cards.en: In essay questions on world history, the influence that trade had on civilizations is sometimes asked. Not only goods but also religions, technologies and even diseases were carried, greatly changing societies everywhere. For example, along the Silk Road, Buddhism spread eastward together with silk and spices. In an answer, if you go beyond listing items and write down what changes they caused, the evaluation rises. Depending on whether by land or sea, the goods that can be carried and the way culture spreads differ.

Now, with globalization advanced, an event in one region ripples across the world within days. That is exactly why knowing the flow of history becomes a compass for living in an age of uncertain outlook. Clues for thinking about the future are, surprisingly, often lying in the distant past.

cards.ja: 幕末に結ばれた不平等条約って、教科書だと一行で終わっちゃうんですけど、実はそこが日本の近代の出発点なんですよね。関税を自分で決められず、外国人が罪を犯しても日本の法律では裁けない。主権国家として認めてもらうために、法律も裁判所も西洋式に整える必要があったんです。条約改正は、外交というより、国の仕組みごと作り直す大仕事でした。最終的に関税自主権が完全に回復したのは、一九一一年のことでした。
cards.en: The unequal treaties concluded in the late Edo period get just one line in textbooks, but actually that is the starting point of Japan's modernity. Japan couldn't set its own tariffs, and even when foreigners committed crimes they couldn't be tried under Japanese law. To be recognized as a sovereign state, it had to arrange its laws and courts in the Western style. Treaty revision was less diplomacy than a huge task of rebuilding the whole machinery of the nation. Tariff autonomy was finally restored in full in 1911.

cards.en: The starting point of the modern international order is said to be the Peace of Westphalia of 1648. Triggered by this treaty, concluded after the Thirty Years' War, the principle spread that a state holds supreme power within its territory and receives no interference from other states. The idea of the sovereign state born in this way was later carried over into the UN Charter as well. However, scenes like the Vienna System, where great powers decide small states' fates, were repeated afterward too.

words.defJa: 立法・行政・司法を別の機関に分けること

It is a mechanism in which the three branches, legislative, executive and judicial, check one another to prevent runaway power. On exams, not to mention the idea itself, even its influence on the US Constitution tends to be asked, so it pays to draw a diagram and output it. However, Japan's parliamentary cabinet system differs somewhat in character from a strict separation. Learning it while comparing with Japan's own system deepens understanding considerably.

words.defJa: 考えや行動が最初から最後まで変わらないこと

cards.ja: 優れた文章には、一貫性という見えない背骨が通っています。たとえば「です・ます調」で書き始めたなら、最後まで同じ調子で通すのが基本です。途中で「である」が混ざると、読者は無意識のうちに違和感を覚えてしまいます。内容の正しさはもちろん、文体が最後まで揃っていればこそ、文章は信頼されるのです。同じ内容でも、語尾や敬語の度合いがぶれるだけで、書き手の信頼度は驚くほど下がってしまいます。
cards.en: Good writing has an invisible backbone called consistency. For example, if you begin in the desu-masu style, the rule is to keep the same tone to the end. If a plain "de aru" creeps in midway, readers feel a sense of discord without realizing it. Not to mention correct content, it is only when the style stays uniform to the end that a text earns trust. Even with the same content, just a wobble in sentence endings or level of politeness lowers the writer's credibility astonishingly.

words.defJa: 強い不安が続き生活に支障が出る心の病気

cards.ja: 夜になると理由のない胸騒ぎがして眠れない。会議の前に手が震え、人混みに出ると息が苦しくなる。こうした症状が日常生活に支障をきたすほど続く場合、不安障害という診断がつくことがあります。トラウマが引き金になるケースもありますが、はっきりした原因が見つからないことも少なくありません。放っておくと悪化しかねないので、気の持ちようと片づけず、早めに専門家へ相談することが大切です。
cards.en: At night you feel an unexplained unease and cannot sleep. Your hands shake before meetings, and your breathing gets hard when you go out into crowds. When such symptoms persist enough to interfere with daily life, a diagnosis of anxiety disorder may be made. Trauma can be the trigger in some cases, but it is not uncommon for no clear cause to be found. Left alone it may well worsen, so it is important to consult a specialist early rather than dismissing it as a matter of attitude.

cards.ja: スピーチで抽象的な話が続くと、聞き手の頭には何も残らない。そこで、「楽器」と言いたいところを、下位語である「チェロ」や「三味線」に置き換えてみる。具体的な言葉が入った途端、情景が浮かび、聞き手の関心が一気に戻ってくるのだ。たとえば「花」より「彼岸花」と言うだけで、聞き手の頭には赤い色まで浮かぶ。ひらめきを待つことなく、上位語に頼りすぎず、一語ずつ具体化する癖をつけるとよい。
cards.en: When abstract talk continues in a speech, nothing stays in the listeners' heads. So where you would say instrument, try swapping in a hyponym such as cello or shamisen. The moment a concrete word enters, a scene comes to mind and the listeners' interest returns all at once. For example, just saying higanbana instead of flower makes even the color red come to the listeners' minds. Without waiting for inspiration, and without leaning too much on hypernyms, get into the habit of making things concrete one word at a time.

cards.en: In the eighteenth-century Atlantic, a triangular trade linking Europe, Africa and the Americas was generating enormous wealth. European merchants carried manufactured goods to Africa, bought slaves there, and shipped them to plantations in the Caribbean and North America. The sugar and cotton grown on the plantations were taken back to Europe and sold off. Behind the prosperity, over ten million people were forced into transport, and it is also pointed out that this deepened the roots of later racial discrimination.

words.defJa: 体を緊張や活動の状態にする神経

cards.ja: 緊張した場面で心臓が高鳴るのは、交感神経が優位になっているからである。体は敵に備えて血圧と心拍を上げ、同時にストレスホルモンのコルチゾールも分泌される。この反応は本来、命を守る働きであるが、会議や試験のたびに過剰に働けば、心身を疲弊させかねない。ゆえに、意識的に呼吸をゆっくり整え、体を休める側の神経の働きを高めることが、日々の安定には欠かせないのだ。深呼吸が効くのは、この切り替えを促すからである。
cards.en: The heart pounds in tense situations because the sympathetic nervous system has become dominant. The body raises blood pressure and heart rate to prepare for an enemy, and at the same time the stress hormone cortisol is also secreted. This reaction is originally a function that protects life, but if it works excessively at every meeting or exam, it could wear out mind and body. Therefore, consciously slowing the breath and raising the activity of the nerves that rest the body is essential to daily stability. Deep breathing works because it prompts this switch.

words.defJa: 農民などが団結して起こす反乱

cards.ja: 日本史の問題で一揆が出たら、まず誰が何に抗議したのかを確かめると整理しやすいです。農民に限らず、武士や信者が主役になる場合もあります。ただ、事件名と年号を丸暗記するだけでは、すぐに頭から抜けてしまいます。原因・主体・結果の三点で表にまとめておくのが、入試対策としてはいちばん確実でしょう。たとえば戦国時代の加賀では、一向宗の信者たちが守護を倒し、約一世紀にわたって自治を続けたことで知られます。
cards.en: When an uprising comes up in a Japanese history question, it is easier to sort out if you first confirm who protested against what. Not only peasants but also warriors and believers sometimes play the leading role. Still, merely memorizing event names and dates by rote makes them slip from your head quickly. Summarizing each in a table of cause, actors and result is probably the surest approach for exam preparation. In Kaga during the Sengoku period, for example, followers of the Ikko sect toppled the governor and are known for sustaining self-rule for about a century.

cards.ja: 江戸時代の人口が三千万人前後で、ほとんど増えなかった理由のひとつは、乳幼児死亡率の高さだったと言われているんですよ。生まれても五歳まで育たない子が珍しくなかったので、七五三のような行事も、そういう背景から生まれたと言われます。ところが明治以降、衛生や栄養が改善されたことに伴って、死亡率が急に下がっていきました。その結果、日本の人口動態は大きく書き換わることになります。
cards.en: It is said that one reason Edo-period Japan's population hovered around thirty million and hardly grew was the high infant mortality rate. It was not uncommon for children not to survive to age five, and events like Shichi-Go-San are also said to have arisen from that background. After Meiji, however, as hygiene and nutrition improved, the death rate dropped sharply. As a result, Japan's demographics were largely rewritten.

words.defJa: 一つの政党だけが政権を握り続ける体制

cards.ja: ソ連や今の中国みたいに、一つの党だけが政権を握り続ける一党独裁って、じつは憲法も議会も三権分立の建前までちゃんとあるんですよ。ただ、党が決めたことには逆らえない仕組みになっているだけで。名前が立派だからといって、中身まで機能しているとは限りませんよね。だから制度の看板より、最後に誰が決めるのかを見たほうがいいんです。選挙の結果より党内の人事のほうが国の行方を左右する場面も、少なくありません。
cards.en: In places like the Soviet Union or China today, where a single party holds on to power, a one-party dictatorship actually has a constitution, a parliament, and even the pretense of the separation of powers. It's just built so that nobody can defy what the party decides. But a grand name doesn't mean the substance actually works, right? So rather than the signboard of the system, it's better to look at who makes the final call. There are also plenty of cases where personnel decisions inside the party steer the country's course more than election results do.

words.defJa: 世界や人生をどうとらえるかという見方

cards.ja: インドを旅していると、「世界観」ってこんなに違うものかと驚くことがあるんですよ。たとえば、人生は一度きりじゃなくて、何度も生まれ変わる輪廻の途中だって、ごく普通に信じている人が多い。今日うまくいかなくても、焦るどころか平然としていて、ご利益を祈って寺院に通う姿もごく自然に見えてきます。自分の常識が唯一のものじゃないと気づけたのが、旅のいちばんの収穫でした。景色より、この気づきのほうが、ずっと長く心に残ります。
cards.en: When traveling in India, I sometimes marvel at how different a worldview can be. For example, plenty of people quite ordinarily believe that life isn't a one-time thing but a stretch of an endless cycle of rebirth. Even if things go badly today, they are calm rather than anxious, and the sight of them going to temples to pray for blessings comes to look entirely natural. Realizing that my own common sense isn't the only one was the greatest harvest of the trip. More than the scenery, this realization stays with me far longer.

words.meaning: Declaration of the Rights of Man
words.defJa: 人間の自由や平等を世に示した宣言

cards.ja: 一七八九年八月、革命のさなかのフランスで人権宣言が採択されました。人は生まれながらに自由で、権利において平等だと述べた第一条は、身分制の社会に突きつけられた挑戦状でした。三権分立の発想も盛り込まれ、のちの世界各国の憲法に大きな手本を示します。とはいえ、当時は女性や奴隷の権利が十分に考えられておらず、その矛盾は後世の運動によって問い直されていきました。この宣言の理念は、今も国際的な議論の出発点になっています。
cards.en: In August 1789, in France amid revolution, the Declaration of the Rights of Man was adopted. Article One, stating that people are born free and equal in rights, was a gauntlet thrown down to a society of fixed ranks. It also incorporated the idea of the separation of powers, and set a great model for the constitutions of many later nations. That said, the rights of women and slaves were not adequately considered at the time, and that contradiction was questioned again through later movements. The ideals of this declaration remain a starting point of international debate today.

cards.en: From the end of the Muromachi period into the Sengoku period, a trend of gekokujo, retainers overthrowing lords and deputy governors displacing governors, spread nationwide. Class barriers grew brittle, and it became an age when, regardless of birth, anyone with ability could rule a domain. Recent research, however, has considerably revised the traditional image that Hojo Soun rose to power in a single generation. Even so, it is beyond doubt that the authority of hereditary succession was shaken.

words.defJa: 中国を世界の中心とみなす考え方

cards.ja: 中華思想っていうのは、ざっくり言うと、中国こそ世界の中心で、周りの国は文明の遅れた周縁だっていう考え方なんですよ。この見方では、中国の皇帝だけが天命を受けて世界を治める存在とされました。皇帝のもとに周辺国が使節を送って貢ぎ物を捧げる朝貢という仕組みも、そこから来ています。朝鮮王朝が自らを「小中華」と称したのが、その一例です。世界観は、自分が中心にいるだけに、どうしても見えにくくなるものです。
cards.en: Sinocentrism, roughly speaking, is the idea that China is the center of the world and the surrounding countries are uncivilized peripheries. In this view, only the Chinese emperor was deemed to receive the mandate of heaven and govern the world. The tribute system, in which neighboring states sent envoys to the emperor and offered gifts, also comes from this. The Joseon dynasty calling itself a little China is one example. A worldview, precisely because you are at its center, inevitably becomes hard to see.

words.defJa: 手当たり次第にいろいろな本を読むこと

cards.ja: 本は一冊を精読するべきだという教えがある。しかし私は、ジャンルを問わず手当たり次第に読む乱読にも、捨てがたい価値があると考えている。無関係に見える分野の知識が頭の中でふいに結びつくとき、ひらめきは向こうからやって来るからだ。ただし、読みっぱなしでは知識がアウトプットされないまま溜まるだけなので、気になった一文を書き留める手間は惜しめない。たまたま手に取った一冊が、人生の方向を変えることもあるのだ。
cards.en: There is a teaching that one should read a single book closely. But I think that indiscriminate reading, reading anything at hand regardless of genre, also has a value that is hard to discard. When knowledge from seemingly unrelated fields suddenly connects in the head, inspiration comes from the other side. However, if you merely read and leave it, knowledge just piles up without being output, so the effort of jotting down a line that caught you cannot be spared. A book picked up by chance can even change the direction of a life.

words.defJa: 商人や品物が行き来する道筋

cards.ja: 海のシルクロードとも呼ばれる交易路が、インド洋に網の目のように広がっていました。季節ごとに向きを変える季節風、つまりモンスーンを利用して、船は半年ごとに東西を行き来しました。インド西岸の港町には、アラブやペルシアの商人が集まり、香辛料や綿織物が運ばれていきました。この海の道があったからこそ、仏教やイスラームといった宗教も、船に乗って遠くまで伝わったのです。それは地図の上の線ではなく、人と物語の通り道だったのです。
cards.en: Trade routes also called the maritime Silk Road spread across the Indian Ocean like a net. Using the seasonal winds that change direction with the season, that is the monsoon, ships traveled back and forth between east and west every half year. In the port towns on India's west coast, Arab and Persian merchants gathered, and spices and cotton textiles were carried onward. It was precisely because of this sea road that religions such as Buddhism and Islam also traveled far by ship. It was not a line on a map but a thoroughfare of people and stories.

cards.ja: 起業家の伝記を読むと、成功談よりも失敗の記録のほうがずっと長いことに気づきます。会社を潰し、撤退を余儀なくされても、また立ち上がる姿はまさに七転び八起きです。ただ、折れない心は生まれつきの才能ではなく、小さな回復を重ねた結果だと言われています。ストレス耐性とは、転ばない力ではなく、起き上がる力のことだと言えそうです。最初の一歩より、倒れたあとの二歩目こそが、その人の底力を映し出すのでしょう。
cards.en: Reading entrepreneurs' biographies, you notice that the record of failures is far longer than the success stories. Even after wrecking a company and being forced to retreat, the way they stand up again is truly falling seven times and rising eight. Still, an unbreakable spirit is said to be the result of piling up small recoveries, not an inborn talent. Stress tolerance, it seems, is not the power never to fall but the power to get back up. More than the first step, the second step after falling is probably what reveals a person's real reserves of strength.

words.meaning: resolve to change; make up one's mind
words.defJa: 強い決意で何かを始めること

cards.ja: 話し下手を何年も嘆いていた同僚が、四十を過ぎて一念発起し、朗読教室の門を叩いた。最初の発表では声が震えて、聞き返される始末だった。それでも三日坊主にならず、毎朝十分、腹から声を出す練習を続けたところ、半年後には会議で堂々と意見を述べるようになっていた。変わるきっかけは、能力よりも、始めるという決断のほうにある。決意そのものより、その翌朝にもう一度立ち上がれるかが、本当の分かれ目なのだろう。
cards.en: A colleague who had lamented his poor speaking for years resolved to change after turning forty and knocked on the door of a reading-aloud class. At his first presentation his voice shook, and he ended up being asked to repeat himself. Even so, he did not quit after three days, and when he kept practicing speaking from the belly for ten minutes every morning, half a year later he was stating his opinions confidently in meetings. What triggers change lies less in ability than in the decision to begin. More than the resolve itself, what truly divides people is probably whether they can get up again the next morning.

words.defJa: 人間の価値や可能性を重んじる考え方

cards.ja: 十四世紀のイタリアで始まったルネサンスの中心には、人文主義があった。知識人たちは、古代ギリシャ・ローマの文献を読み直し、神中心の世界観から、人間の可能性を探る方向へと関心を移した。人間の尊厳を、神の権威と並べて語ろうとする姿勢が、この時代に広がったのである。ペトラルカやエラスムスは、その代表的な存在として知られる。印刷術の普及に伴って、彼らの著作は国境を越えて読まれ、宗教改革にも間接的に影響を及ぼした。
cards.en: At the center of the Renaissance, which began in fourteenth-century Italy, was humanism. Intellectuals reread the texts of ancient Greece and Rome and shifted their interest from a God-centered worldview toward exploring human potential. An attitude of speaking of human dignity alongside divine authority spread in this era. Petrarch and Erasmus are known as representative figures. With the spread of printing, their works were read across borders and indirectly influenced the Reformation as well.

cards.en: "Humans die, Socrates is human, therefore Socrates dies." That's the famous example of a syllogism. As long as the form is right, a conclusion necessarily follows, but if the premises are off, it can end up a plausible-sounding yet wrong story. Something like "people who don't study get bad grades, he gets bad grades, so he doesn't study" sounds plausible but is actually a logical error. It's worth remembering that the correctness of form and the correctness of content are different things.

That is because information not connected to meaning or usage is a low-priority fragment for the brain. Research has shown that the testing effect, which inserts the act of recalling, gives better retention than study that merely rereads. Of course, there are also basics, like the multiplication table, that are better acquired through repetition. If you want to remember, stop reading and move to the side that solves problems.

That said, such records also carry their authors' bias, so cross-checking several of them is indispensable. Preserving and publishing the records is the first step toward that.

cards.en: In October 1929, triggered by the crash of stock prices on the New York Stock Exchange, the Great Depression began. The unemployed filled the streets, banks fell one after another, and world trade shrank rapidly, spreading a sense of opacity about the outlook. Countries raised tariffs to protect themselves and turned to bloc economies, but this only deepened international conflict. The serious slump is said to lie behind Japan, Germany and Italy later leaning toward territorial expansion. The lessons were also put to use in later financial regulation and the building of social security.

The very idea of escaping by sheer willpower can be off the mark. What is needed is not to blame the person but to change the environment and for those around them to support them by listening attentively. Although recovery has a long plateau, rebuilding step by step is well worth it.

cards.en: Polishing prose means not adding modifiers but cutting them. The more you pile on words, as in “a very wonderful beautiful view,” the more the scene actually blurs. If the nouns and verbs are exact, the scene comes across without any rhetorical elaboration. On the other hand, a shift of just one position in a modifying word can change the meaning of a sentence. “A beautiful mother's friend” could leave the reader unsure whether it is the mother or the friend who is beautiful.

cards.en: In modern kana orthography, particles such as ha, he and wo still preserve a mismatch between sound and writing. For instance, the ha in watashi-wa is actually read as wa, isn’t it. The modern kana usage announced in 1946 greatly simplified the old spellings, but it did not erase this mismatch. If you read old books, knowing the traditional spellings is indispensable. Once you learn the history of writing that runs back to man’yogana, you can see there is a reason even for that odd mismatch.

cards.en: “I make my child eat vegetables.” This “saseru” is the typical form of the Japanese causative. It is grammar that expresses a relationship in which someone makes, or ends up making, someone do something, and along with the passive it is an item learners easily stumble over. What is interesting is that it is also used, as in “to make someone laugh,” when one moves another's feelings unintentionally, and in slang “don't make me laugh” becomes a sarcastic “how ridiculous.” Further, putting it in the “saserareru” form adds even a feeling of grievance or victimhood, as in “being made to do it.”

In Japanese-language teaching, practice of counting beats while clapping is said to be effective. It also appears in loanwords such as “beddo” and “baggu,” and shapes the pronunciation of foreign words.

words.defJa: 他国の領土を自国に組み入れること。

If you rephrase the 1910 annexation of Korea as a “merger,” for instance, you could give the impression that there was an agreement between equals. Within this word is contained a relationship of power, in which one side incorporated the other into its own territory. So a speaker needs to confirm a term's definition before using it. A way of speaking that is unaware of the weight of words not only loses the listener's trust but makes people doubt the speaker's ethics.

The more a person believes they still have margin, the more they face others' words with an attitude of attentive listening. cards.en: In world history exams, terms concerning the handling of diplomatic rights are asked almost without fail. For example, under the Second Japan-Korea Agreement of 1905, the Korean Empire was deprived of its diplomatic rights and was in effect placed under Japanese control. What matters here is that, unlike annexation, it was not completely incorporated into the territory. If you grasp the differences in terms, memorizing the years also becomes much easier.

words.defJa: 他国に操られ、実権のない政権。

cards.ja: 1932年、日本は中国東北部に満州国を建て、清朝最後の皇帝・溥儀を元首の座に据えました。形のうえでは独立国家でしたが、実権は関東軍が握っており、典型的な傀儡政権だったと評価されています。国際連盟はリットン調査団を送り、1933年に満州国を認めない勧告を採択しました。日本はこれに反発して、連盟を脱退しています。名目と実態のずれ、そして実態が不透明な国家のからくりを見抜くことが、歴史を読むうえでの基本になります。
cards.en: In 1932, Japan set up the state of Manchukuo in northeastern China and installed Puyi, the last emperor of the Qing, as head of state. It was an independent state in form, but real power was held by the Kwantung Army, and it is assessed as a typical puppet regime. The League of Nations sent the Lytton Commission and in 1933 adopted a recommendation not to recognize Manchukuo. Japan reacted against this and withdrew from the League. Seeing through the gap between nominal and actual, and through the workings of a state whose reality is opaque, is the basis for reading history.

words.defJa: 昔からの言い伝えや、受け継がれた事柄。

cards.ja: 日本各地には、一夜にして城が築かれたという伝承が残っています。もちろん史実としては疑わしいのですが、そうした話が語り継がれてきたこと自体が、土地の人々の記憶を映しています。文字を持たない時代ほど、口伝えの物語は歴史の貴重な手がかりになりました。ただし一次史料と突き合わせないまま信じ込むと、事実を取り違えかねません。こうした話は、真偽を問う前に、なぜ語られたのかを問うべき素材なのです。
cards.en: Across Japan, there remain legends that a castle was built overnight. Of course they are doubtful as history, but the very fact that such tales have been passed down reflects the memory of the local people. The further back in time to an age without writing, the more precious a clue oral stories become to history. Still, if you believe them without checking against primary sources, you might mistake the facts. Such a tale is material about which, before asking whether it is true, we should ask why it was told.

がかりになりました。ただし
えかねません。こうした
cards.tipJa: 「伝承が残る」「口頭伝承」。語り継がれてきた話。
cards.enTarget: Across Japan, there remain legends that a castle was built overnight.

words.defJa: 神仏を信じ、深く敬う心。

cards.ja: 浄土真宗の教えでは、救いは修行の量ではなく、信心によって決まると説かれます。親鸞は、自分の力で悟ろうとする心が、かえって慢心を生みかねないと考えました。そこで、阿弥陀仏への信にすべてを委ねる道を、人々に示したのです。これは他力本願の考え方に通じるもので、努力を否定するのではなく、努力の限界を見つめる態度でした。難しい理屈より、素直に手を合わせる心こそが、大切にされたのです。
cards.en: In the teaching of Jodo Shinshu, salvation is said to be decided not by the amount of practice but by faith. Shinran thought that a mind trying to attain enlightenment by its own power could instead breed arrogance. So he showed people a path of entrusting everything to trust in Amida Buddha. This connected with the idea of reliance on other-power, and was an attitude not of denying effort but of looking squarely at its limits. More than difficult theory, a heart that simply puts its palms together was what was treasured.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「信心深い」。教えを信じて敬う心。親鸞の他力の教えと結びつく。
cards.enTarget: In the teaching of Jodo Shinshu, salvation is said to be decided not by the amount of practice but by faith.

words.defJa: 相手の話に、心を込めて耳を傾けること。

cards.ja: コーチングの基本は、話すことではなく傾聴にあります。相手の話をさえぎることなく、うなずきや短い相づちで、聞いていることを態度で伝えるのです。以心伝心を期待せず、伝わるように示すことが大切です。人は、自分の考えを言葉にして聞いてもらえたとき、答えを自分で見つけ出すことがよくあります。聞き上手になる近道は、話し上手を目指すことではなく、沈黙を怖がらないことなのです。
cards.en: The basis of coaching lies not in speaking but in attentive listening. Without interrupting the other person, you convey through nods and brief responses that you are listening. It is important not to expect telepathic understanding but to show it so it comes across. When people have a chance to put their own thoughts into words and be heard, they often find the answer themselves. The shortcut to becoming a good listener is not aiming to be a good speaker but not fearing silence.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

すことがよくあります。
がらないことなのです。
cards.tipJa: 「傾聴の姿勢」。相手の話を遮らず、心から聞くこと。
cards.enTarget: The basis of coaching lies not in speaking but in attentive listening.

words.defJa: 本筋とは別の、ついでの話。

cards.ja: 話の途中で余談を挟むと、聞き手の気持ちがふっとゆるみます。ただし長すぎると本題を見失わせてしまうので、三十秒ほどでおさめるのがコツです。数字の話が続いたあとに、取材先で聞いた小さなエピソードを一つ添えるだけで、空気が変わります。脱線から本題へ戻るときは、「さて」と一言入れるだけで、聞き手の注意が戻ってきます。以心伝心を当てにすることなく、戻る合図を声に出すのです。
cards.en: Slipping a digression into the middle of a talk gently loosens the listener's mood. If it is too long, though, it makes them lose sight of the main topic, so the knack is to keep it to about thirty seconds. After a run of numbers, simply adding one small episode you heard on assignment changes the atmosphere. When you return from the tangent to the main subject, just inserting a single 'well then' brings the listener's attention back. Without counting on telepathic understanding, you say the cue to return out loud.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ちがふっとゆるみます。ただし
ほどでおさめるのがコツです。
cards.tipJa: 「余談ですが」。本題から離れた話。聞き手の息抜きにもなる。
cards.enTarget: Slipping a digression into the middle of a talk gently loosens the listener's mood.

words.defJa: 借りたものを返さなければならない義務。

cards.ja: 歴史の語りでは、債務を人の物語に置き換えると、聞き手の理解が一気に深まります。たとえば第一次世界大戦後のドイツの賠償金は、巨額の借金として国民の暮らしを圧迫し、ハイパーインフレの一因ともなりました。当時の日記や物価表といった一次史料をもとに、パンの値段が一日のうちに変わった生活を描くほうが、数字を並べるより胸に迫ります。数字は事実の骨組みであり、物語を通して初めて血が通うのです。
cards.en: In telling history, replacing debt with a human story deepens the listener's understanding all at once. For example, Germany's reparations after the First World War pressed on people's lives as an enormous burden of borrowing and became one cause of hyperinflation. Drawing on primary sources like diaries and price tables of the time, depicting a life in which the price of bread changed within a single day stirs the heart more than lining up figures. Numbers are the skeleton of fact, and only through story does blood flow into them.

cards.tipJa: 「債務を抱える」「債務超過」。返済の義務。
cards.enTarget: In telling history, replacing debt with a human story deepens the listener's understanding all at once.

words.defJa: 仏の教えを修め、広める出家者。

cards.ja: 仏教の僧侶は、もともとは家を出て、托鉢で食べ物を受けながら修行する人々でした。日本では、鎌倉時代に親鸞が妻帯の道を示して以来、結婚して寺を継ぐ住職も珍しくなくなりました。同じ出家者といっても、戒律の守り方は国や宗派によって大きく違うのです。インドで生まれた教えが各地に広がる過程で、暮らしの形も、土地の風土に合わせて変わっていきました。タイと日本とでは、日常の姿がずいぶん異なります。
cards.en: Buddhist monks were originally people who left home and trained while receiving food through alms rounds. In Japan, ever since Shinran showed a path of marrying in the Kamakura period, it has become not uncommon for head priests to marry and inherit a temple. Even among those who have left home, how the precepts are kept differs greatly by country and school. As the teaching born in India spread to various places, the form of daily life also changed to suit the local climate. Their everyday appearance differs considerably between Thailand and Japan.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: わっていきました。タイと
cards.tipJa: 「僧侶の修行」。出家して仏道を修める人。
cards.enTarget: Buddhist monks were originally people who left home and trained while receiving food through alms rounds.

words.defJa: 他の言語から取り入れて使う言葉。

cards.ja: 日本語には、外国語から入ってきた借用語がとても多く、カタカナ語に限らず試験でも頻出です。たとえば「アルバイト」はドイツ語、「パン」はポルトガル語が語源だとされます。英語だと思って使っていた言葉が、実は別の言語に由来すると知ると、覚え方が変わるでしょう。ただし「ノートパソコン」のように、日本で独自に作られた和製英語もあるので、注意が必要です。漢字を音として借りた万葉仮名の昔から、日本語は外の文化を取り込んできました。
cards.en: Japanese has very many loanwords that came in from foreign languages, and they appear often on exams, not only katakana words. For example, 'arubaito' is said to derive from German and 'pan' from Portuguese. When you learn that a word you thought was English actually comes from another language, the way you remember it will change. But there are also Japan-made English coinages like 'notopasokon,' so caution is needed. Since the days of man'yogana, which borrowed kanji for their sounds, Japanese has been taking in outside culture.

cards.enTarget: Japanese has very many loanwords that came in from foreign languages, and they appear often on exams, not only katakana words.

words.defJa: 寺を預かる、その寺の長である僧。

cards.ja: 寺の朝は早い。まだ暗いうちに鐘が鳴り、住職は祈りを込めて、冷え切った広い本堂でゆっくりと経を読み始める。参拝者の去った境内を掃き、檀家の悩みに耳を傾ける日課は、一見すると地味であり、派手な出来事など何も起こらない。だが、その繰り返しのなかにこそ、教えが生きていると言えるだろう。僧侶の務めとは、特別な悟りを誇ることではなく、同じ一日を丁寧に重ねることなのである。
cards.en: Mornings at a temple come early. While it is still dark the bell rings, and the head priest begins to chant sutras in the main hall with prayer in his voice. The daily routine of sweeping the grounds once worshippers have gone and lending an ear to the troubles of the temple's parishioners looks modest at first glance, and nothing flashy ever happens. Yet it is precisely within that repetition that the teaching can be said to live. A monk's duty is not to boast of special enlightenment but to lay one ordinary day upon another with care.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「〜寺の住職」。寺の責任者。僧侶一般とは区別される。
cards.enTarget: While it is still dark the bell rings, and the head priest begins to chant sutras in the main hall with prayer in his voice.

words.defJa: 大きな出来事のあとに残る影響。

cards.ja: 1929年に始まった世界恐慌の余波は、やがて大西洋を越えて日本にも及んだ。生糸の輸出が急減し、農村では娘の身売りが出るほどの深刻な不況が広がったとされる。各国は自国産業を守るべく関税を引き上げ、保護貿易の壁が世界を分断していった。不況の長期化は、各地で急進的な政治勢力が伸びる土壌ともなった。経済危機が国境を越えて連鎖する構図は、今日の金融不安にも通じるものがある。
cards.en: The aftershocks of the Great Depression that began in 1929 eventually crossed the Atlantic and reached Japan as well. Raw-silk exports plunged, and a severe slump is said to have spread to farming villages, to the point that daughters were sold off. To protect their own industries, countries raised tariffs, and walls of protective trade split the world. The prolonged slump also became fertile ground for radical political forces to grow in various places. The pattern of economic crisis chaining across borders has something in common with financial anxieties today.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「〜の余波を受ける」。大事件のあとに続く影響。
cards.enTarget: The aftershocks of the Great Depression that began in 1929 eventually crossed the Atlantic and reached Japan as well.

words.defJa: 気が進まず、面倒に感じるさま。

cards.ja: 春先になると、朝ふとんから出るのが億劫になる、という声が増える。気温の変化に伴って、日照時間や体内時計が揺らぐためだとされる。仏教に目を向ければ、この語の「劫」は、古代インドで宇宙の始まりから終わりまでを数えた、きわめて長い時間の単位を指す。「億」がつくのだから、途方もない時間を意味し、そこから、面倒で気が進まないという感覚へと意味が移ったとされる。語の旅路を知ると、朝のだるさにも少し余裕を持って向き合える。
cards.en: As early spring arrives, there is a growing chorus that getting out of the futon in the morning has become a drag. It is said that with changes in temperature, the hours of daylight and the body clock are thrown off. Looking to Buddhism, the 'kalpa' in this word refers to an extremely long unit of time, used in ancient India to count from the start of the universe to its end. Since 'hundred million' is attached, it meant an immense stretch of time, and from there the sense is said to have shifted to a feeling of bother and reluctance. Knowing the word's journey, you can face morning sluggishness with a bit more composure.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「〜するのが億劫だ」。気が重くて動き出すのが面倒なさま。
cards.enTarget: As early spring arrives, there is a growing chorus that getting out of the futon in the morning has become a drag.

words.defJa: 言葉で人を説得する技を研究する学問。

cards.ja: 修辞学って、古代ギリシャで生まれた、説得のための学問なんですよ。アリストテレスは、人を動かす要素を、話し手の人柄、聞き手の感情、話の論理の三つに整理しました。三段論法の基本を作ったのも彼ですしね。どれほど論理だけで押しても人は動かないし、感情だけでも長続きしません。だから二千年以上もたった今でも、ビジネス向けのプレゼンの本は、この古い枠組みをもとにしているわけです。
cards.en: Rhetoric is a discipline of persuasion born in ancient Greece, you know. Aristotle sorted the elements that move people into three: the speaker's character, the listener's emotions, and the logic of the talk. He's also the one who laid the basics of the syllogism. Pushing with logic alone doesn't move people, and emotion alone doesn't last. That's why, even two thousand years on, books on presentations are still built on this old framework.

みをもとにしているわけです。
cards.tipJa: 「古代ギリシャの修辞学」。人柄・感情・論理で説得を整理した学問。
cards.enTarget: Rhetoric is a discipline of persuasion born in ancient Greece, you know.

words.defJa: 成長が思うように進まないこと。

cards.ja: 努力しているのに結果が出ない。この伸び悩みの時期は、三日坊主で終わる人にも、長く続けた人にも等しく訪れる。多くの人は、結果が出ないからといって才能の限界を疑い、あっさり手を引いてしまう。しかし成長は直線ではなく階段状に進むものであり、平坦に見える期間にも内側では力が蓄えられている。停滞に見えるものが、実は次の跳躍の助走であったと気づくのは、たいてい後になってからだ。
cards.en: You are trying hard, yet no results appear. This period of stagnation comes equally to those who quit after three days and to those who persisted for a long time. Many people, just because results don't come, doubt the limits of their talent and give up readily. But growth proceeds not in a straight line but in steps, and even in a stretch that looks flat, strength is being stored inside. It is usually only later that we notice what looked like stagnation was in fact a run-up to the next leap.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「伸び悩みの時期」「成績が伸び悩む」。成長が頭打ちになる状態。
cards.enTarget: This period of stagnation comes equally to those who quit after three days and to those who persisted for a long time.

words.defJa: あるものの代わりをつとめること。

cards.ja: AIが人間の仕事を奪うと言われますが、実際に起きているのは、仕事そのものではなく作業の代替です。たとえば議事録づくりは、音声認識と要約の技術のおかげで、数分で終わるようになりました。ところが、会議で何を決めるべきかという問いまでは、機械に肩代わりさせるわけにはいきません。置き換わるのは手順であって、判断の責任は人に残るのです。この線引きを間違えると、便利さが倫理の問題にすり替わりかねません。
cards.en: People say AI will take human jobs, but what is actually happening is the replacement of tasks, not of the work itself. Writing up meeting minutes, for example, now takes only minutes thanks to speech recognition and summarization technology. But the question of what a meeting ought to decide is not something we can hand over to a machine. What gets replaced is the procedure; responsibility for judgment stays with people. Get this dividing line wrong, and convenience could slip into becoming a question of ethics.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: わるようになりました。ところが、
わりさせるわけにはいきません。
cards.tipJa: 「代替の＋名詞」「代替案」など。作業の置き換えを指す。
cards.enTarget: People say AI will take human jobs, but what is actually happening is the replacement of tasks, not of the work itself.

words.defJa: 短い時間、ちょっと眠ること。

cards.ja: 昼ご飯を食べたあとって、どうしても眠くなるじゃないですか。そんなときは無理に粘るより、十五分ぐらい仮眠をとったほうが、午後の仕事の効率は、ぐっと上がるんですよ。ただし三十分を超えて寝ちゃうと、かえって頭がぼんやりしてしまいます。体内時計が乱れる原因にもなるので、長く寝るなら夜にまとめるに限りますね。ちなみに僕は、昼休みに机に突っ伏して寝るのがいちばん落ち着きます。
cards.en: You get sleepy after lunch no matter what, right? Rather than forcing yourself to push through, taking a fifteen-minute nap will raise your afternoon efficiency. But if you sleep past thirty minutes, your head actually ends up foggy. It can also throw off your body clock, so if you want to sleep long, nothing beats saving it for the night. By the way, during my lunch break I'm most at ease dozing with my head down on the desk.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

くなるじゃないですか。そんなときは
がぼんやりしてしまいます。

cards.enTarget: Rather than forcing yourself to push through, taking a fifteen-minute nap will raise your afternoon efficiency.

words.meaning: relying on Amida's vow; relying on others
words.defJa: 阿弥陀仏の誓いにすがる教え。人任せ。

cards.ja: 他力本願という言葉は、いまでは人任せの怠け心を叱るときに使われる。だが本来は、阿弥陀仏の誓願に身をゆだねる浄土教の教えであり、決して軽い意味ではなかった。自分の力では悟りに届かないと見極めればこそ、人は深く頭を下げるのである。この徹底した謙虚さは、努力の放棄とは似て非なるものであり、むしろ最も厳しい自己点検といってよい。己の無力を見つめ抜いた末に、信心は静かに立ち上がってくる。
cards.en: Today the word tariki hongan is used to scold someone for lazily leaving things to others. Originally, though, it was a Pure Land teaching of entrusting oneself to Amida Buddha's vow, and it carried no such light meaning. Precisely because one has seen that one cannot reach enlightenment by one's own strength, one bows deeply. This thoroughgoing humility is quite different from giving up effort; if anything, it is the harshest form of self-examination. Only after staring down one's own powerlessness does faith quietly rise.

cards.tipJa: 俗用の「人任せ」と本来の仏教語の意味の落差。「ばこそ」と相性がよい。
cards.sense: 仏教語としての本義
cards.enTarget: Today the word tariki hongan is used to scold someone for lazily leaving things to others.

words.defJa: 大国が他国を戦わせて争うこと。

cards.ja: 冷戦期の朝鮮半島やベトナムは、しばしば代理戦争の舞台と呼ばれてきた。米ソは直接には砲火を交えず、同盟国や武装勢力に武器と資金を送り込んだのである。核兵器を持つ大国同士が正面衝突しようものなら、人類そのものが危うくなるからだ。たとえ停戦が成立しても、背後にある対立の構図は簡単には消えない。大国の冷静な計算ほど、現地の人々にとって、これほど残酷なものはなかった。
cards.en: The Korean Peninsula and Vietnam of the Cold War era have often been called stages for proxy wars. The United States and the Soviet Union did not exchange fire directly; they poured weapons and funds into allies and armed groups. If two nuclear-armed powers were ever to collide head-on, humanity itself would be in danger. Even when a ceasefire is reached, the structure of rivalry behind it does not vanish easily. For the people on the ground, nothing was as cruel as the cool calculations of the great powers.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

うくなるからだ。たとえ
cards.tipJa: 「〜の代理戦争」「代理戦争の舞台」。大国の対立が他国で戦われる形。
cards.enTarget: The Korean Peninsula and Vietnam of the Cold War era have often been called stages for proxy wars.

words.defJa: 経験を通じて、身につけること。

cards.ja: 自転車の乗り方を、説明書だけで覚えた人はいませんよね。バランスの感覚は、何度も転んで初めて体得できる知識だからです。学習科学では、これを手続き記憶と呼び、言葉で説明できる知識とは別の仕組みで保存されると考えます。試験勉強では、数学に限らず、問題を解く量が決定的に重要になります。修練を重ねるうちに、いつのまにか、頭で考えなくても手が動く段階に入っていくのです。
cards.en: No one has ever learned to ride a bicycle from an instruction manual alone, have they? The sense of balance is knowledge you can only master through experience after falling many times. Learning science calls this procedural memory and holds that it is stored by a different mechanism from knowledge you can put into words. In exam study, not only in math, the sheer volume of problems you solve becomes decisively important. As you pile up training, you enter a stage where your hands move without your head having to think.

ねるうちに、いつのまにか、
cards.tipJa: 「技を体得する」。頭で知るのではなく、体で覚えて自分のものにする。
cards.enTarget: The sense of balance is knowledge you can only master through experience after falling many times.

words.defJa: 国の代表として外国へ派遣される一行。

cards.ja: 岩倉使節団の話を人前でするときは、まず数字を一つだけ示すと、聞き手が一気に引き込まれます。1871年に横浜を出発したこの一行は、二年近くにわたって欧米を回りました。この旅の当初の狙いは不平等条約の改正の下交渉でしたが、成果は思うように上がりませんでした。大久保利通や伊藤博文といった後の指導者が含まれていた点を伝えれば、旅の重みが伝わります。細かな訪問先を並べるよりも、何を見て何を持ち帰ったかを語るほうが、物語として残ります。
cards.en: When you tell the story of the Iwakura Mission in public, first showing just one number draws listeners in at once. This party, which left Yokohama in 1871, toured Europe and America over nearly two years. The trip's original aim was preliminary negotiation for revising the unequal treaties, but the results did not come as hoped. If you convey that future leaders such as Okubo Toshimichi and Ito Hirobumi were included, the weight of the journey comes across. Rather than listing detailed destinations, telling what they saw and what they brought back stays with people as a story.

cards.tipJa: 「岩倉使節団」。国を代表して派遣される団体。
cards.enTarget: When you tell the story of the Iwakura Mission in public, first showing just one number draws listeners in at once.

words.defJa: 戦いをいったん止めること。

cards.ja: 試験で紛らわしいのが、停戦と終戦と講和の違いです。これは、戦闘行為をいったん止める合意で、戦争そのものが法的に終わるわけではありません。たとえば、冷戦期の代理戦争でもあった朝鮮戦争の休戦協定は、今も平和条約に置き換わっておらず、半島は技術的には戦争状態にあります。一方、講和は、国家間で戦争状態を正式に終える条約を指します。用語を区別したうえで覚えておけば、記述問題でも迷わずに答えられるでしょう。
cards.en: What tends to be confusing on exams is the difference between ceasefire, end of war, and peace settlement. It is an agreement to halt fighting for the time being, and it does not mean the war itself ends legally. For example, the armistice of the Korean War, which was also a Cold War proxy war, has still not been replaced by a peace treaty, and the peninsula is technically in a state of war. A peace settlement, on the other hand, refers to a treaty that formally ends the state of war between states. If you memorize the terms after distinguishing them, you will be able to answer essay questions without hesitation.

cards.enTarget: What tends to be confusing on exams is the difference between ceasefire, end of war, and peace settlement.

words.defJa: 技や心を、繰り返し鍛え磨くこと。

cards.ja: どんな分野でも、名人と呼ばれる人は、修練の量が桁違いです。ただし、ただ長く続ければいいわけではありません。心理学者エリクソンの研究では、課題の難しさを少しずつ上げながら、フィードバックを受け続ける練習が、上達に結びつくとされています。これは、伸びしろがどこにあるかを見極めて、そこに集中するということでもあります。惰性の反復は、時間だけが過ぎていく作業にすぎません。
cards.en: In any field, those called masters have an overwhelming amount of training. But it is not enough simply to continue for a long time. In the psychologist Ericsson's research, practice that raises task difficulty a little at a time while continuing to receive feedback is said to lead to improvement. This also means identifying where your room for growth lies and concentrating there. Repetition out of inertia is nothing more than work in which only time passes.

cards.enTarget: In any field, those called masters have an overwhelming amount of training.

words.defJa: 関税などで自国の産業を守る考え方。

cards.ja: 関税の壁を高くして自国産業を守る保護主義は、不況のたびに支持を集める。国内の雇用を守るという目的は、一見すると正当であり、有権者にも分かりやすい。しかし世界恐慌後の経験が示すように、各国が一斉に壁を築けば、世界の貿易は縮み、不況は深まるばかりだ。結局、短期の痛みを避けようとする政策が、長期の損失を招くのである。守るという言葉の甘さを疑うことが、経済を論じる出発点となる。
cards.en: Protectionism, which raises tariff walls to shield domestic industry, gains support with every downturn. The aim of protecting domestic jobs is at first glance legitimate and easy for voters to grasp. But as the experience after the Great Depression shows, if every country builds walls at once, world trade shrinks and the slump only deepens. In the end, a policy that tries to avoid short-term pain invites long-term loss. Doubting the sweetness of the word 'protect' is the starting point for discussing economics.

cards.tipJa: 「保護主義に傾く」。関税や規制で国内産業を守る政策思想。
cards.enTarget: Protectionism, which raises tariff walls to shield domestic industry, gains support with every downturn.

words.defJa: 思想などを、実際の行いで形に表すこと。

cards.ja: ガンジーって、非暴力という思想を頭で語っただけの人じゃないですよね。塩の行進のように、自分の体で動いてみせた人なんです。教えを体現するっていうのは、言葉と行動の一貫性を保つってことなんですよ。インドの哲学でも、理解するだけで終わることなく、生き方に落とし込むことが重んじられてきました。口だけの賢者というより、黙って実践する人のほうが、よっぽど説得力があります。
cards.en: Gandhi wasn't someone who just talked about nonviolence in his head, right? Like the Salt March, he was someone who showed it by moving with his own body. To embody a teaching means keeping words and actions consistent. In Indian philosophy too, it has been valued not to stop at understanding but to bring it down into how one lives. A person who quietly practices is far more persuasive than a sage who is all talk.

cards.tipJa: 「理念を体現する」。思想や教えを行動で形にすること。
cards.enTarget: To embody a teaching means keeping words and actions consistent.

words.defJa: 軍隊が他国に攻め入ること。

cards.ja: 1941年6月、ドイツ軍は独ソ不可侵条約を破り、ソ連への侵攻を開始しました。バルバロッサ作戦と呼ばれたこの作戦は、数百万規模の兵力を動員した、史上最大級の陸戦だったとされています。当初は電撃的に進んだものの、冬の到来と補給線の伸びきりで、ドイツ軍は次第に動きが鈍っていきました。独裁者の判断が現場の声を封じた点も、見逃せません。一党独裁のもとでは、誤りを正す仕組みが働きにくいのです。
cards.en: In June 1941, the German army broke the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact and began its invasion of the Soviet Union. This operation, called Barbarossa, is said to have been one of the largest land battles in history, mobilizing forces in the millions. Although it advanced like lightning at first, the arrival of winter and overextended supply lines gradually slowed the German army. The fact that the dictator's judgment silenced voices from the front cannot be overlooked either. Under one-party dictatorship, mechanisms for correcting errors are slow to work.

だったとされています。

cards.enTarget: In June 1941, the German army broke the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact and began its invasion of the Soviet Union.

words.defJa: 周りに人がいるほど、人が動かなくなる現象。

cards.ja: 道で人が倒れていても、周りに人が多いほど、誰も助けに行かない。この現象を傍観者効果と呼びます。1964年にニューヨークで起きた事件をきっかけに、心理学者のラタネとダーリーが実験で調べました。結果は、目撃者が多いほど、一人ひとりが責任を感じにくくなり、行動に移すまでの時間が長くなるというものでした。倫理や道徳を説くだけでは行動は変わらず、「そこの青いシャツの方、救急車を呼んでください」と、特定の人を指名して頼むほうが有効だとされます。
cards.en: Even if a person has collapsed in the street, the more people there are around, the less anyone goes to help. This phenomenon is called the bystander effect. Prompted by an incident in New York in 1964, the psychologists Latane and Darley investigated it through experiments. The result was that the more witnesses there are, the less each individual feels responsible and the longer it takes to act. Merely preaching ethics and morality does not change behavior; it is said to be more effective to single out a particular person and ask, 'You in the blue shirt, call an ambulance.'

くなるというものでした。
cards.tipJa: 「傍観者効果が働く」。目撃者が多いほど、個人の責任感が薄れる。
cards.enTarget: This phenomenon is called the bystander effect.

words.defJa: 音や事の終わった後に残る味わい。

cards.ja: いい話し手は、たいてい、最後の一言のあとに、わざと間をあけます。その数秒の長い沈黙のなかで、聞き手は話の内容をかみしめるのです。華やかな修辞を並べるより、沈黙のほうが雄弁なときもあります。最後の最後まで言葉を詰め込んでしまうと、余韻が生まれる隙間すらなくなり、話は聞いたそばから流れていきます。話し終えた直後の静けさや、客席の空気までが、話の一部だといえます。
cards.en: A good speaker deliberately leaves a pause after the final word. In those few seconds of silence, the listener savors the content of the talk. At times silence is more eloquent than a string of showy rhetoric. If you cram in words right to the end, there is not even a gap left for a lingering resonance to arise. Even the stillness right after a talk ends is part of the talk.

cards.tipJa: 「余韻に浸る／を残す」。終わったあとに残る響きや感じ。
cards.enTarget: If you cram in words right to the end, there is not even a gap left for a lingering resonance to arise.

words.defJa: 物事を行う順番を決める、重要さの順。

cards.ja: やることが多すぎて動けないときは、優先順位をつけるところから始めましょう。有名なのが、緊急度と重要度で仕事を四つに分ける方法で、本当に時間を使うべきなのは、緊急ではないが重要な項目です。たとえば、体調管理や学習の習慣づくりは、今日やらなくても困らない代わりに、後回しにすると大きな損失になります。反対に、通知への即答のような緊急で重要でない作業が、一日を食いつぶしてしまいがちです。三日坊主を恐れず、紙に書き出して眺めるだけで、頭のなかが驚くほど整理されます。
cards.en: When there is too much to do and you cannot move, start by setting priorities. A well-known method divides tasks into four by urgency and importance, and what you should truly spend time on is the items that are important but not urgent. For example, managing your health and building study habits will not trouble you if skipped today, but postponing them means a large loss. Conversely, work that is urgent but unimportant, like answering notifications instantly, tends to eat up the day. Without fearing quitting after three days, just writing it out on paper and looking at it tidies up your head surprisingly well.

cards.enTarget: When there is too much to do and you cannot move, start by setting priorities.

words.defJa: 必要な分を超えて余っていること。

cards.ja: 歴史の授業で習った話なんですけど、農業が発達して余剰の食べ物が生まれたことが、文明の出発点だったそうですよ。みんなが食料づくりに追われなくなれば、役人や職人、僧侶みたいに、畑に出ない人たちを養えるようになるじゃないですか。余った分があればこそ、文字も都市も税も生まれたわけです。逆に言えば、そうした余裕は決して当たり前ではなく、不作が続いただけで、社会の仕組みは簡単にきしみます。
cards.en: This is something I learned in a history class, but apparently the origin of civilization was that agriculture developed and a surplus of food came into being. Once everyone is no longer chased by the work of producing food, you can support people who don't go out to the fields, like officials, craftsmen, and monks, right? It's precisely because there was a surplus that writing, cities and taxes came into being. Conversely, a few bad harvests in a row are enough to make the structure of society creak.

cards.enTarget: This is something I learned in a history class, but apparently the origin of civilization was that agriculture developed and a surplus of food came into being.

words.defJa: 物事の意味やこつを深く理解すること。

cards.ja: 話し方の上達に、近道はありません。腹式呼吸も間の取り方も、本を読んだだけでは身につかず、何度も声に出して確かめる反復を通じて、ようやく会得できるものです。最初のうちは録音した自分の声を聞くのもつらいのですが、そこを越えると聞き手の反応が見えてきます。伸び悩みを感じる時期こそ、基礎に立ち返る好機にほかなりません。練習の量が、ある日ふっと質に変わる瞬間があるのです。
cards.en: There is no shortcut to improving how you speak. Neither diaphragmatic breathing nor timing can be acquired by reading a book alone; you finally master them only through the repetition of saying them aloud. At first even listening to a recording of your own voice is painful, but once you get past that, the listener's reactions come into view. A period when you feel you have stalled is precisely the chance to return to the basics. There comes a moment when, one day, the quantity of practice suddenly turns into quality.

cards.tipJa: 「コツを会得する」。時間をかけて身につけ、理解すること。
cards.enTarget: Neither diaphragmatic breathing nor timing can be acquired by reading a book alone; you finally master them only through the repetition of saying them aloud.

words.meaning: ending a sentence on a noun
words.defJa: 文を名詞で終える表現技法。

cards.ja: 俳句や短歌では、体言止めという技法がよく使われます。たとえば「夏草や兵どもが夢の跡」は、最後を名詞で終えることで、余韻を深く残しています。述語を言い切らない分、読者は情景を自分の想像で補うことになるのです。新聞の見出しが「首相、来月訪米」と短く結ぶのも、同じ仕組みを活用したもので、読み手の目に素早く届きます。ただし多用すると、文章全体が単調になりかねません。
cards.en: In haiku and tanka, the technique called ending on a noun is often used. For example, the famous line about summer grass, the traces of warriors' dreams, ends on a noun and so leaves a deep lingering resonance. Because the predicate is not stated outright, the reader supplies the scene from their own imagination. Newspaper headlines that end tersely, as in 'Prime Minister, U.S. visit next month,' use the same mechanism. Used too often, however, the whole text can become monotonous.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 俳句や見出しで余韻や簡潔さを出す技法。使いすぎに注意。
cards.enTarget: In haiku and tanka, the technique called ending on a noun is often used.

words.defJa: 語順を入れ替えて感情を強める表現。

cards.ja: 「美しい、この夜景は」のように、述語を先に置く倒置法は、感情を強く押し出す技法である。演説などでは、「忘れてはならない、この教訓を」といった言い回しが、あえて使われることがある。語順を崩すことで、聞き手の注意は前に置かれた言葉に集まり、余韻も深くなる。ただし多用すれば、文章全体がわざとらしくなりかねない。日常会話での倒置が、とっさの感情の表れであるのとは対照的だ。
cards.en: The inversion technique, which puts the predicate first as in 'Beautiful, this night view,' is a device that pushes emotion forward strongly. In speeches and the like, phrasings such as 'We must not forget, this lesson' are sometimes used deliberately. By breaking the word order, the listener's attention gathers on the words placed first, and the lingering resonance deepens too. Overused, however, the whole text can become affected. This contrasts with inversion in everyday talk, which is an outburst of spontaneous feeling.

cards.tipJa: 「倒置法を用いる」。述語を先に出して強調する修辞技法。
cards.enTarget: The inversion technique, which puts the predicate first as in 'Beautiful, this night view,' is a device that pushes emotion forward strongly.

words.defJa: 知識や人格を、努力して磨くこと。

cards.ja: インドの伝統では、学ぶことと自分を磨くことは、もともと切り離されていませんでした。弟子が師のもとで暮らし、掃除や炊事という日々の修練をこなしながら知を受け取る修養のかたちが、古くから続いてきたのです。教室で知識だけを仕入れる現代の勉強法とは、ずいぶん違いますよね。けれども、自己管理や習慣づくりが注目される今、こうした生活全体を使った学びが、見直されつつあります。試験の点数を超えた学び方を、考え直すきっかけになるでしょう。
cards.en: In the Indian tradition, learning and polishing oneself were originally not separated. A form of self-cultivation, in which a disciple lived with a teacher and received knowledge while carrying out the daily discipline of cleaning and cooking, has continued since ancient times. It's quite different from modern study methods that just stock up on knowledge in a classroom, isn't it? Yet now that self-management and habit-building are drawing attention, this kind of learning that uses the whole of life is being reconsidered. It may become an occasion to rethink ways of learning beyond exam scores.

すきっかけになるでしょう。
cards.tipJa: 「人格の修養」。知識だけでなく人格を磨くこと。
cards.enTarget: A form of self-cultivation, in which a disciple lived with a teacher and received knowledge while carrying out the daily discipline of cleaning and cooking, has continued since ancient times.

words.defJa: 関税などで国内産業を守る貿易政策。

cards.ja: 自由貿易と保護貿易の対比は、世界史でも政経でも頻出のテーマです。国が関税を高くして輸入品を割高にし、国内の産業を育てる政策のことを指します。19世紀のドイツの経済学者リストは、育ちきっていない産業を守るために必要だと唱えました。一方、イギリスは先に工業化を終えたからこそ、自由貿易を強く主張したのです。世界恐慌のあとに各国が壁を高くした場面でも、同じ論理が顔を出します。
cards.en: The contrast between free trade and protective trade is a frequent theme in both world history and politics-economics. It refers to a policy in which the state raises tariffs, makes imports expensive and nurtures domestic industry. The nineteenth-century German economist List argued it was necessary to protect industries not yet fully grown. Britain, on the other hand, argued strongly for free trade precisely because it had finished industrializing first. The same logic shows up when countries raised their walls after the Great Depression.

cards.tipJa: 「自由貿易」と対にして覚える。関税で国内産業を育てる政策。
cards.enTarget: The contrast between free trade and protective trade is a frequent theme in both world history and politics-economics.

words.defJa: 体にそなわった、時間を測る仕組み。

cards.ja: 久しぶりに海外旅行から帰ってきたら、一週間くらい頭がぼーっとしませんでしたか。あれ、体内時計がまだ現地の時間で動いてるからなんですよね。朝の光を浴びると、この時計はちょっとずつリセットされます。逆に、夜遅くまでスマホをつけっぱなしにしていると、時計が後ろにずれていっちゃうんです。カーテンを開けて朝日を浴びるのを三日坊主で終わらせないことが、いちばんのコツですよ。
cards.en: After coming back from overseas travel, didn't your head feel foggy for about a week? That's because your body clock is still running on local time over there. When you take in morning light, this clock is reset little by little. Conversely, if you leave your phone on until late at night, the clock drifts backwards. The biggest trick is not letting the habit of getting morning sun fizzle out after three days.

words.defJa: 伝統や秩序を重んじ、急な変化を避ける立場。

cards.ja: 保守主義の父と呼ばれるのは、18世紀イギリスの政治家エドマンド・バークです。彼はフランス革命を批判し、人間の理性だけで社会を作り直そうとする試みは危うい、と論じました。伝統や慣習には、長い時間をかけて試されてきた知恵が蓄えられている、という考え方です。もっとも、これは何も変えないという意味ではなく、改革は現実に沿って少しずつ進めるべきだという主張でした。彼が求めたのは、過去と現在をつなぐ一貫性だったのです。
cards.en: The father of conservatism is said to be Edmund Burke, an eighteenth-century British politician. He criticized the French Revolution and argued that attempts to remake society on human reason alone are dangerous. It is the view that traditions and customs store wisdom that has been tested over a long time. This did not mean changing nothing, though; his claim was that reform should proceed little by little in line with reality. What he sought was a consistency linking past and present.

ruby: エドマンド・バークです。
cards.tipJa: 「バークと保守主義」。伝統を重んじ、改革は漸進的にと考える立場。
cards.enTarget: The father of conservatism is said to be Edmund Burke, an eighteenth-century British politician.

words.defJa: 進歩が止まったように見える時期。

cards.ja: 筋力トレーニングを始めて三か月、体重もバーベルの重さも、ぴたりと動かなくなった。いわゆる停滞期である。専門家によれば、体が負荷に慣れ、同じ刺激では変化が起きにくくなる自然な現象であり、才能の限界を意味するわけではない。重さや回数を状態に応じて変え、刺激に変化をつければ、再び成長が動き出すことが多い。ここで手を止めた人ほど、三日坊主の烙印を自分に押してしまうのだ。
cards.en: Three months after starting strength training, both body weight and the weight on the barbell stopped moving altogether. It is what is called a plateau. According to specialists, it is a natural phenomenon in which the body gets used to the load and changes become hard to produce with the same stimulus, and it does not mean the limit of your talent. If you vary weight and repetitions according to your condition and change the stimulus, growth often starts moving again. The people who stop here are the ones who brand themselves quitters.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: かなくなった。いわゆる
cards.tipJa: 「停滞期に入る」。ダイエットや筋トレで進歩が止まる時期。
cards.enTarget: It is what is called a plateau.

words.defJa: 仏や死者に供え物をして祈ること。

cards.ja: 日本の寺では、役目を終えた針や人形、ときには筆まで供養する習わしがあります。その本来の意味は、仏や先祖に食べ物や花や祈りを捧げることでした。ところが日本では、万物に心が宿るという感覚が重なり、感謝を込めて別れを告げる儀式へと広がったのです。インドの仏教がそのままの形で伝わったわけではなく、土地の信仰と溶け合いながら姿を変えました。モノへのそうした祈りは、そうした長い混ざり合いの結果といえます。
cards.en: At Japanese temples there is a custom of holding memorial rites even for needles and dolls that have finished their service, and at times even for brushes. Its original meaning was to offer food, flowers and prayers to the Buddha and ancestors. In Japan, however, a feeling that a spirit dwells in all things overlapped with it, and it spread into a ritual of bidding farewell with gratitude. It is not that Indian Buddhism arrived in its original form; it changed shape while blending with local beliefs. Rites for objects can be called the result of that long mixing.

がったのです。インドの
えました。モノへのそうした
cards.tipJa: 「先祖を供養する」「人形供養」。祈りと感謝を捧げる儀式。
cards.enTarget: At Japanese temples there is a custom of holding memorial rites even for needles and dolls that have finished their service, and at times even for brushes.

words.defJa: 言葉なしに心が通じ合うこと。

cards.ja: 日本のビジネス現場では、以心伝心を美徳とする空気が長く続いてきた。言葉にしなくても察し合うことが、円滑な協働の証とみなされたのである。ところが、外国人社員が増えるにつれ、職場のなかで、この暗黙の了解が通用しない場面が目立ち始めた。指示の不透明さによるやり直しを課題に挙げる企業も、少なくない。従来の察する文化を守りながらも、言語化の習慣を意識的に取り入れる動きが広がりつつある。
cards.en: In Japanese workplaces, an atmosphere that prizes tacit understanding has long persisted. Sensing each other's intent without putting it into words was taken as proof of smooth collaboration. But as foreign employees have increased, situations where this unspoken understanding fails to work have become conspicuous. Not a few companies cite rework caused by unclear instructions as a problem. While preserving the traditional culture of intuiting, a movement to adopt the habit of putting things into words is spreading.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: とみなされたのである。ところが、
cards.tipJa: 「以心伝心で通じる」。日本の職場文化を論じる報道調。
cards.enTarget: In Japanese workplaces, an atmosphere that prizes tacit understanding has long persisted.

words.defJa: 考えや計画を実際の形にすること

cards.ja: 目標は、具体化しない限り、ただの願望で終わります。「日本語が上手になりたい」ではなく、「三か月後に、五分間の自己紹介をやり遂げる」と決めるのです。ここまで絞り込めば、今日やるべきことが、おのずと見えてきます。そうして一歩ずつ体得したものは、のちの伸びしろにもなっていくでしょう。曖昧な夢に期限と数字を与えるだけで、頭の中の景色は驚くほど鮮明になり、行動のハードルも下がっていきます。
cards.en: A goal ends up as a mere wish unless you make it concrete. Instead of 'I want to get good at Japanese,' you decide, 'in three months, I will carry off a five-minute self-introduction'. Once you narrow it down this far, what you should do today comes into view naturally. What you master step by step in that way will also become room for further growth later. Merely giving a vague dream a deadline and a number makes the scenery in your head astonishingly clear, and the hurdle to action drops as well.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: やるべきことが、おのずと
びしろにもなっていくでしょう。
cards.tipJa: 「計画を具体化する」「構想の具体化」。「〜化」でサ変動詞的に働く名詞。
cards.enTarget: A goal ends up as a mere wish unless you make it concrete.

words.defJa: 罪の償いを軽くするとして教会が売った証書

cards.ja: 16世紀、ローマ教会が売り出した免罪符は、聖堂の建設資金を集める手段でもあった。これに疑問を投げかけたルターが、1517年に九十五か条の論題を発表する。ルターの怒りは、信仰の証が金で買えるかのように扱われる風潮そのものに向けられていた。論題を皮切りに改革の動きは各地へ広がり、その余波は欧州全体に及んだ。現代では、「これさえあれば責任を問われない」という口実の意味で、この語が比喩的にも使われる。
cards.en: In the sixteenth century, the indulgences the Roman Church put on sale were also a means of raising funds to build a cathedral. Luther, who questioned this, published his Ninety-Five Theses in 1517. Luther's anger was aimed at the very climate in which a token of faith was treated as something money could buy. Starting with the theses, the reform movement spread to many places, and its aftershocks reached all of Europe. Today the word is also used figuratively to mean an excuse of the kind, 'with this alone, no one can hold me responsible'.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 本来は宗教改革の語。「〜は免罪符にならない」と比喩で使う用法も多い。
cards.enTarget: In the sixteenth century, the indulgences the Roman Church put on sale were also a means of raising funds to build a cathedral.

words.defJa: 進行中の作業の途中に入ること

cards.ja: 勉強の最中に通知が入ると、元の集中状態へ戻るまでに二十分ほどかかるといわれます。小さな割り込みでも、頭の中の作業メモリは確実に消耗するのです。そのため、効率のいい人ほど、机に向かう前にスマホを別の部屋に置いてしまいます。創造性を要する課題ほど、途切れない時間の確保が成果を分けるでしょう。通知を切る、机の上を片づける、そんな小さな環境づくりが、最も確実な集中の技術なのです。
cards.en: It is said that when a notification arrives in the middle of studying, it takes about twenty minutes to return to the original state of concentration. Even a small interruption reliably drains the working memory in your head. That is why efficient people put their phones in another room before sitting at the desk. The more a task demands creativity, the more securing uninterrupted time will decide the result. Turning off notifications and tidying the desk, such small environment-building is the most reliable technique for concentration.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ほどかかるといわれます。
cards.tipJa: 名詞「割り込み」。「割り込みが入る」。機械の割り込み処理とも同じ語。
cards.enTarget: Even a small interruption reliably drains the working memory in your head.

words.defJa: 組織や仕組みを組み替えること

cards.ja: 半導体業界では、ここ数年、企業の再編が相次いでいます。巨額の開発費を一社で背負いきれなくなり、合併や提携に活路を見いだす動きが増えたからです。その一方で、買収には各国の規制当局が目を光らせ、承認に数年を要する例も珍しくありません。その結果、どの国のどの企業が主導権を握るのかが、今後の産業地図を大きく塗り替えるでしょう。代替の利かない部品が多い業界だけに、一つの判断の余波が世界中に広がるのです。
cards.en: In the semiconductor industry, corporate reorganizations have followed one after another over the past few years. This is because more companies, unable to shoulder enormous development costs alone, are finding a way out in mergers and partnerships. On the other hand, regulators in each country keep a sharp eye on acquisitions, and it is not rare for approval to take several years. As a result, which company in which country takes the initiative will greatly redraw the industrial map from here on. Precisely because it is an industry with many irreplaceable parts, the aftershock of a single decision spreads around the world.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「業界再編」「事業再編」と使う。合併・統合・分割などで形を組み替えること。
cards.enTarget: In the semiconductor industry, corporate reorganizations have followed one after another over the past few years.

words.defJa: 物事の方向が分かれる重大な境目

cards.ja: 歴史の分水嶺って、あとから振り返らないと分からないものですよね。たとえば1914年のサラエボの銃声も、その瞬間は地方で起きた事件にすぎなかったはずです。それが同盟関係を通じて余波を広げ、気づけば世界大戦ですよ。当事者は、まさか自分たちが歴史の曲がり角に立っているなんて、思ってもいなかったでしょうね。だからこそ、いまの私たちも、気づかないまま大きな分かれ道を通り過ぎているのかもしれませんね。
cards.en: The watersheds of history can't be recognized unless you look back later, can they? For example, the gunshots in Sarajevo in 1914 too must have been, at that moment, nothing more than an incident in a provincial place. Through alliance ties they spread their aftershocks, and before you knew it, it was a world war. The people involved surely never imagined they were standing at a turning point in history. That is why we too, now, may be passing a major fork in the road without noticing.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

にすぎなかったはずです。それが
ってもいなかったでしょうね。だからこそ、いまの

cards.tipJa: 「歴史の分水嶺」「運命の分水嶺」。山の尾根で水が分かれる所から転じた比喩。
cards.enTarget: The watersheds of history can't be recognized unless you look back later, can they?

words.defJa: 集めた富を改めて人々に配り直すこと

cards.ja: 再分配とは、豊かな者から取り上げて貧しい者に配るという単純な話ではない。社会が生み出した余剰を、どの程度、どのような仕組みで人々に戻すかをめぐって、思想は大きく分かれてきた。共産主義のように徹底した平等を掲げる立場もあれば、機会の平等だけで足りるとする立場もある。いずれにしても、配り方を誤れば、働く意欲そのものを損ないかねない。何を公平と呼ぶかという問いに、唯一の正解がないことが、この議論を終わりにくくしている。
cards.en: Redistribution is not the simple matter of taking from the rich and handing it to the poor. Over how much of the surplus a society produces should be returned to people, and by what mechanism, schools of thought have split widely. There are positions that champion thorough equality, as in communism, and positions that hold equality of opportunity alone is enough. Either way, if the distribution is done wrongly, it may damage the very will to work. The fact that the question of what to call fair has no single right answer makes this debate hard to bring to an end.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: もある。いずれにしても、
cards.tipJa: 「所得の再分配」「再分配政策」。税や社会保障で富を配り直す経済の語。
cards.enTarget: Redistribution is not the simple matter of taking from the rich and handing it to the poor.

words.defJa: 関心が自分の内面に向かいやすい性格

cards.ja: 内向型の人は、人付き合いが苦手なのではなく、刺激の多い場所で消耗しやすいだけだと説明されることが多い。静かな環境で一人考える時間を確保したほうが、創造性が高まるという指摘もある。ところが、職場では発言の多さが評価されがちで、内省を重んじる人ほど損をしかねない。近年は、会議の進め方を見直し、事前に意見を書面で集める企業も出てきた。静かな力を活かせる仕組みづくりが、チーム全体の成果にもつながるとみられている。
cards.en: Introverts are often explained as people who are not bad at socializing but simply tire easily in highly stimulating places. It has also been pointed out that securing time to think alone in a quiet environment raises creativity. Yet in workplaces, talkativeness tends to be rewarded, and people who value introspection may end up at a disadvantage. In recent years, some companies have reviewed how meetings run and gather opinions in writing beforehand. Building a system that can make use of quiet strengths is also seen as leading to better results for the whole team.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: にもつながるとみられている。
cards.tipJa: 外向型と対にする。「内向型人間」のように人を指す名詞としても使う。
cards.enTarget: Introverts are often explained as people who are not bad at socializing but simply tire easily in highly stimulating places.

words.defJa: 空域を軍事的に支配する力

cards.ja: 現代の戦争では、地上で戦う前に、まず制空権を握れるかどうかが勝敗を左右します。1940年のバトル・オブ・ブリテンで、ドイツ空軍は上陸作戦に先立って、イギリス上空の主導権を奪おうとしました。しかし、イギリスの戦闘機部隊が粘り強く抵抗し、目標は果たせませんでした。その結果、英本土への侵攻計画は断念されたのです。空を押さえた側が、地上の戦いでも主導権を握るという教訓は、のちの戦争にも受け継がれました。
cards.en: In modern war, before fighting on the ground, whether you can seize air supremacy first decides victory or defeat. In the Battle of Britain in 1940, the German air force tried to wrest control of the skies over Britain prior to a landing operation. But Britain's fighter squadrons resisted tenaciously, and the goal was not achieved. As a result, the plan to invade the British mainland was abandoned. The lesson that the side that holds the sky also takes the initiative in the ground fight was carried over into later wars.

cards.enTarget: In modern war, before fighting on the ground, whether you can seize air supremacy first decides victory or defeat.

words.defJa: 君主を置かず国民が主権を持つ政治体制

cards.ja: 共和制を民主主義と同じ意味だと思い込んだばかりに、試験で点を落とす人は少なくありません。その本質は、君主がいないこと、そして権力が一人に集中しないことにあります。古代ローマでは、執政官が二人置かれ、元老院がその働きを支えました。この仕組みを押さえておけば、のちの帝政との違いも、すっきり整理できるはずです。権力を分け合う工夫こそ、この制度が長く語られてきた理由なのだと、年表の裏側から読み取ってください。
cards.en: Quite a few people lose points on exams simply because they assumed a republic means the same as democracy. Its essence lies in having no monarch and in power not being concentrated in one person. In ancient Rome two consuls were appointed, and the Senate supported their work. If you grasp this mechanism, you should be able to sort out the difference from the later empire neatly. Please read, from behind the chronology, that the ingenuity of sharing power is the reason this system has been discussed for so long.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: しないことにあります。
cards.tipJa: 「帝政」「君主制」と対にして覚える。「共和国」は国そのものを指す。
cards.enTarget: Quite a few people lose points on exams simply because they assumed a republic means the same as democracy.

words.defJa: 領土の一部を他国に譲り渡すこと

cards.ja: アヘン戦争に敗れた清は、1842年の南京条約で、香港島をイギリスに割譲しました。領土を手放すという決断は、国の威信を大きく傷つけるものでした。条約の文面は短くても、そこで決められた領土の移り変わりは、住民の暮らしを根こそぎ変えてしまいました。これを皮切りに、列強の要求が相次ぐ時代が幕を開けたのです。その余波は、二十世紀に入っても、東アジアの国際関係に影を落とし続けました。
cards.en: Defeated in the Opium War, the Qing ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain in the Treaty of Nanking in 1842. The decision to give up territory badly damaged the nation's prestige. Though the wording of a treaty may be short, the shift of territory decided there changed the lives of the residents from the roots. Starting with this, an era in which the great powers' demands came one after another opened. Its aftershocks kept casting a shadow over East Asian international relations even after the twentieth century began.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: えてしまいました。これを
cards.tipJa: 「領土を割譲する」「割譲地」。条約で領土を譲る歴史・外交の語。
cards.enTarget: Defeated in the Opium War, the Qing ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain in the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.

words.defJa: 大脳の前方にあり思考を司る部分

cards.ja: 前頭葉は、計画を立て、衝動を抑える、人間らしい働きの中枢といわれる。ところが、疲労やストレスが重なると、真っ先に働きが鈍るのもこの領域である。そうなると、冷静な判断力は揺らぎ、わかっていながらも目先の快楽に流されてしまう。睡眠不足の翌日に、つい甘いものへ手が伸びるのも、この働きが落ちている証拠だといわれる。意志の弱さを責める前に、脳を休ませる工夫を考えたい。
cards.en: The frontal lobe is said to be the center of distinctly human functions, such as planning and suppressing impulses. Yet when fatigue and stress pile up, it is also this region whose function dulls first. Then calm judgment wavers, and even knowing better, we are swept along by immediate pleasure. The way a hand reaches for sweets after a short night's sleep is also said to be evidence that this function has dropped. Before blaming weakness of will, we should think about ways to rest the brain.

ruby: らぎ、わかっていながらも
cards.tipJa: 脳の部位名。「前頭葉の働き」「前頭葉が衰える」。計画・抑制と結びつく。
cards.enTarget: The frontal lobe is said to be the center of distinctly human functions, such as planning and suppressing impulses.

words.defJa: 他人より優れていると感じる気持ち

cards.ja: 他人より上に立ちたいという欲求は、思いのほか根が深く、本人にもなかなか自覚しにくい。人は資格や肩書きを手にした瞬間に、周囲を見下ろすような、ささやかな優越感を覚えてしまうものだ。しかし、その快感に身を任せるほど、物事を見る判断力は静かに鈍っていく。自分の中に生まれた小さな高ぶりに気づくには、日々の静かな内省が欠かせない。その高ぶりは、劣等感の裏返しにほかならないのである。
cards.en: The urge to stand above others runs deeper than we expect, and is hard even for the person himself to recognize. The moment people obtain a qualification or a title, they tend to feel a faint sense of superiority. Yet the more they surrender to that pleasure, the more quietly their judgment in seeing things dulls. To notice the small swelling of pride arising within us, daily introspection is indispensable. That pride is nothing other than the flip side of an inferiority complex.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

しにほかならないのである。
cards.tipJa: 優越感を「覚える」「抱く」と言う。劣等感と対になる心理語。
cards.enTarget: The moment people obtain a qualification or a title, they tend to feel a faint sense of superiority.

words.defJa: きわめて短い一瞬の時間

cards.ja: 仏教でいう刹那は、七十五分の一秒ほどとされる、きわめて短い時間の単位である。しかし、この短さを知ったところで、体得したことにはならない。昨日の悩みも、明日の不安も、突きつめれば、いま浮かんでいる思考の連なりにすぎない。心はその一瞬ごとに生まれては消え、その連なりが「私」という感覚をつくっているという。そう思って見つめると、いま交わした言葉の余韻すら、すでに過去のものになっている。
cards.en: In Buddhism, the ksana is a very short unit of time, said to be about one seventy-fifth of a second. But merely knowing how short it is does not mean you have truly embodied it. Yesterday's worries and tomorrow's anxieties are, in the end, nothing more than a chain of thoughts floating up now. The mind is said to arise and vanish with each such instant, and the chain of them creates the sense of 'I'. Looking at it that way, even the lingering resonance of the words just exchanged has already become the past.

したことにはならない。
をつくっているという。そう
cards.tipJa: 仏教語の時間の最小単位。「刹那的」は今だけを追う意で、日常語化した。
cards.enTarget: In Buddhism, the ksana is a very short unit of time, said to be about one seventy-fifth of a second.

words.defJa: 強大な力を持つ複数の国々

cards.ja: 歴史を語る上で、列強という言葉は、ただの「強い国々」と訳してはもったいない。この語には、他国を従わせる力を持つ複数の大国が、互いに牽制し合っているという構図が含まれている。たとえば清が領土の割譲を余儀なくされた例は、その力関係を象徴している。使節団を送って学ぼうとした当時の日本は、その構図の中で必死に立ち位置を探っていた。用語の背景まで説明できてこそ、聞き手の記憶に残る歴史の語りになる。
cards.en: When talking about history, it is a waste to translate 'reppo' merely as 'strong countries'. The word contains the picture of several major powers, able to subjugate other nations, checking one another. The case of Qing China being forced to cede territory, for instance, symbolizes that balance of power. Japan at the time, which sent a mission abroad to learn, was desperately seeking its position within that picture. Only when you can explain even the background of a term does it become a telling of history that stays in the listener's memory.

cards.tipJa: 「欧米列強」「列強の仲間入り」。帝国主義期の大国群を指す歴史語。
cards.enTarget: When talking about history, it is a waste to translate 'reppo' merely as 'strong countries'.

words.defJa: すでに発表されている関連の研究

cards.ja: 論文を書くとき、まず最初に取りかかるべきは先行研究の整理です。すでに誰が何を明らかにしたのかを知らないまま始めると、他人がすでに通った道を、もう一度ゼロから歩くことになりかねません。心理学では、のちに再現性の低さが問題になった研究も少なくありません。そのため、一本の論文を鵜呑みにせず、複数の結果を突き合わせる姿勢が求められます。これは学問に限らず、日々の学習にも通じる考え方です。
cards.en: When writing a paper, the first thing to tackle is organizing the prior research. If you start without knowing who has already shown what, you may end up walking the road others have already trodden. In psychology, there are quite a few studies whose low reproducibility became a problem. So an attitude of not swallowing a single paper whole, and instead cross-checking multiple results, is required. This applies not only to scholarship but also to daily learning.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: くことになりかねません。
なくありません。そのため、
cards.tipJa: 「先行研究を踏まえる」「先行研究を整理する」と使う。論文の定型語。
cards.enTarget: When writing a paper, the first thing to tackle is organizing the prior research.

words.defJa: 経済や技術が高度に発達した国

cards.ja: 先進国と呼ばれる国だって、昔からずっと豊かだったわけじゃないんですよね。たとえば明治の日本は、不平等な条約に苦しみながら、列強に追いつこうと、それはもう必死でした。教育にも、工場にも、鉄道にも、ありったけの力を注ぎ込んだじゃないですか。今の豊かさは、当たり前どころか、そうした長い積み重ねの結果なんです。そう思うと、いまは貧しい後発の国にだって、伸びしろは十分すぎるほどあるはずですよ。
cards.en: Even countries called developed nations haven't always been wealthy. For example, Meiji Japan, suffering under unequal treaties, was desperate to catch up with the great powers. They poured every bit of strength into education and factories, didn't they? Today's affluence is far from a given; it's the result of that long accumulation. Thinking about it that way, even latecomer countries that are poor now should have plenty of room to grow.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: かだったわけじゃないんですよね。たとえば
いつこうと、それはもう
すぎるほどあるはずですよ。
cards.tipJa: 「発展途上国」「後発国」と対比される。「先進国首脳会議」のような複合語でも使う。
cards.enTarget: Even countries called developed nations haven't always been wealthy.

words.defJa: 財産を共有し平等な社会を目指す思想

cards.ja: 冷戦期、共産主義陣営と資本主義陣営の対立は、直接の戦火を避けながら、各地の代理戦争という形で現れた。朝鮮半島やベトナムでは、内戦に大国が介入し、多くの犠牲を生んだ。1991年のソ連崩壊をもって、東西対立は一つの区切りを迎える。イデオロギーの違いが、ふつうの人々の暮らしや国境線までも動かしたことは、あらためて強調しておく必要がある。しかし、その遺産は、今も国際関係に影を落としている。
cards.en: During the Cold War, the confrontation between the communist and capitalist camps avoided direct combat and appeared in the form of proxy wars in various places. On the Korean Peninsula and in Vietnam, great powers intervened in civil wars, producing many casualties. With the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, the East-West confrontation reached a turning point. It needs to be stressed again that differences in ideology moved even the lives of ordinary people and the borders on the map. Yet its legacy still casts a shadow over international relations today.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: かしたことは、あらためて
cards.tipJa: 「共産主義陣営」「共産主義国家」と使う。資本主義・社会主義と区別して覚える。
cards.enTarget: During the Cold War, the confrontation between the communist and capitalist camps avoided direct combat and appeared in the form of proxy wars in various places.

words.defJa: 互いに励まし合って向上すること

cards.ja: 切磋琢磨とは、骨や玉を磨くように、互いに励まし合いながら、己を高めていくことをいう。競い合う相手がいればこそ、人は自分でも気づかなかった伸びしろに出会える。同じ志をもつ仲間の成長を、自分のことのように喜べるとき、人は嫉妬ではなく刺激を受け取れるようになる。ただし、それは他力本願とは、まったく別のものだ。自分の足で立とうとする者同士の間でしか、この関係は成り立たないからである。
cards.en: Sessa-takuma means improving oneself by encouraging one another, as one polishes bone or jade. Precisely because there is a rival to compete with, a person meets room for growth they had not noticed themselves. When one can rejoice in a companion's growth as if it were one's own, one comes to receive stimulation rather than jealousy. However, that is different from relying on others. This relationship holds only between people who try to stand on their own feet.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: れるようになる。ただし、それは
cards.tipJa: 四字熟語。「切磋琢磨し合う」「切磋琢磨する仲間」。骨角と玉石を磨く意から。
cards.enTarget: Sessa-takuma means improving oneself by encouraging one another, as one polishes bone or jade.

words.reading: ふくこうかんしんけい
words.defJa: 体を休息へ導く自律神経

cards.ja: 緊張で眠れない夜は、副交感神経をうまく働かせることがカギです。ゆっくり息を吐くと、心拍が落ち着き、体が休息モードへ切り替わっていきます。逆に、寝る直前までスマホを見っぱなしにしていると、刺激が脳に入り続け、体内時計まで乱れてしまいます。依存症とは言えないまでも、寝室に持ち込まない工夫は、試す価値があります。一日の終わりを整えることが、翌日の集中力を決めるといっても言いすぎではありません。
cards.en: On nights you can't sleep from tension, the key is to engage the parasympathetic nervous system well. When you exhale slowly, your heart rate settles and your body gradually switches to rest mode. Conversely, if you keep staring at your phone until just before bed, stimulation keeps entering the brain and even your body clock gets disrupted. Even if it can't be called an addiction, keeping it out of the bedroom is worth trying. It is no exaggeration to say that how you settle the end of the day decides tomorrow's concentration.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ふくこうかんしんけい
かせることがカギです。ゆっくり
っぱなしにしていると、
いすぎではありません。
cards.tipJa: 交感神経と対になる自律神経。「副交感神経が優位になる」と使う。
cards.enTarget: On nights you can't sleep from tension, the key is to engage the parasympathetic nervous system well.

words.defJa: 海上での軍事的な支配権

cards.ja: 歴史を語る上で、制海権という言葉は、地図の上の線ではなく、海を行き交う船の動きとして描くと伝わりやすい。たとえば1905年の日本海海戦で日本がバルチック艦隊を破ると、ロシアは海からの増援の望みを失い、講和へと傾いた。この一戦の余波は、のちの割譲交渉の席にまで及んだ。聞き手が地図を頭に描ける話し方こそ、歴史を語る技術である。用語の背景まで説明できてこそ、聞き手の記憶に残る歴史の語りになる。
cards.en: When talking about history, the word 'command of the sea' comes across better if you depict it not as lines on a map but as the movement of ships sailing the waters. For example, when Japan defeated the Baltic Fleet at the Battle of Tsushima in 1905, Russia lost hope of reinforcements by sea and leaned toward peace. The aftershock of that single battle reached even the table of the later territorial-cession negotiations. A way of speaking that lets listeners picture the map in their heads is the very skill of telling history. Only when you can explain even the background of a term does it become a telling of history that stays in the listener's memory.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「制海権を握る／失う」。海上交通と海戦の主導権を指す軍事・歴史語。
cards.enTarget: When talking about history, the word 'command of the sea' comes across better if you depict it not as lines on a map but as the movement of ships sailing the waters.

words.defJa: 物事の内部にもとから存在すること

cards.ja: 難しい思想を話すときは、比喩を一つ持っておくと強い。たとえばインド哲学の内在という考えは、「波は海の外から来るのではなく、海そのものの動きだ」と言えば、一瞬で伝わる。この発想に立てば、神を探しに遠くへ旅する必要はなく、探している当の自分こそが答えの在りかとなる。アートマンとブラフマンの一致という核心も、この比喩に乗せれば、会得しやすくなるだろう。ただし、比喩はあくまで入口にすぎず、そこから先は自分で確かめるほかない。
cards.en: When speaking about a difficult idea, it helps to keep one metaphor in hand. For example, the Indian-philosophical idea of immanence comes across instantly if you say, 'a wave doesn't come from outside the sea; it is the movement of the sea itself'. From this standpoint, there is no need to travel far to look for God; the very self that is searching becomes the place where the answer lies. The core of the unity of Atman and Brahman, too, becomes easier to grasp when carried on this metaphor. However, a metaphor is only a doorway, and from there on you have no choice but to verify it yourself.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: りかとなる。アートマンとブラフマンの
しやすくなるだろう。ただし、
cards.tipJa: 「超越」の反対語。神や真理が世界・自己の内にあるという思想の語。
cards.enTarget: For example, the Indian-philosophical idea of immanence comes across instantly if you say, 'a wave doesn't come from outside the sea; it is the movement of the sea itself'.

words.defJa: その土地に古くから住んでいた人々

cards.ja: 文章を書くとき、一語の選び方で読み手の受け取り方は大きく変わる。たとえば北米の先住民を語る際、「発見」を「到達」に置き換えるだけでも、文の視点は一瞬で入れ替わる。入植者の側から見た歴史に慣れていると、そこに潜む先入観には、なかなか気づきにくいものだ。とはいえ、言い換えさえすれば済むという単純な話ではなく、問われているのは語り手の姿勢である。誰の目線で語っているのかを自覚してこそ、文章に説得力が生まれる。
cards.en: When you write, a single word choice greatly changes how readers receive it. For example, when speaking of the indigenous peoples of North America, merely replacing 'discovery' with 'arrival' flips the viewpoint of a sentence in an instant. If you are used to history seen from the settlers' side, the preconceptions lurking there are hard to notice. That said, it is not as simple as just rephrasing; what is being tested is the speaker's stance. Only when you are aware of whose eyes you are speaking through does your writing gain persuasive force.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: づきにくいものだ。とはいえ、
cards.tipJa: 「先住民族」とも言う。語の選び方が視点を決めるという文脈で使われる名詞。
cards.enTarget: For example, when speaking of the indigenous peoples of North America, merely replacing 'discovery' with 'arrival' flips the viewpoint of a sentence in an instant.

words.defJa: 引用や言葉のもとになった書物

cards.ja: 「以心伝心」という言葉の出典は、禅の書物にあります。釈迦が花を掲げると、弟子の迦葉だけが微笑んだという「拈華微笑」の伝承とも、結びつけて語られてきました。言葉を抜きにして心から心へ真理が伝わる、という意味は、そこから広がったものです。このように由来をたどると、慣用句が急に立体的に見えてきます。背景を知っていれば、会話の中で故事を引くときにも、自信を持って意味を説明できるようになります。
cards.en: The source of the phrase 'ishin-denshin' lies in Zen writings. It has also been discussed in connection with the tradition of 'nenge-mishō,' in which, when the Buddha held up a flower, only his disciple Kasyapa smiled. The meaning that truth passes from heart to heart without words spread from there. Tracing an origin like this makes an idiom suddenly look three-dimensional. If you know the background, you can explain the meaning with confidence even when you cite an old tale in conversation.
