cards.enTarget: The essence of the Industrial Revolution lay not in the invention of machines themselves but in the leap in productivity.

words.defJa: 母音の声が消えるように発音されること

cards.ja: 日本語の「です」や「ます」の母音が、実際にはほとんど聞こえないことに気づいたことはありますか。これは母音の無声化と呼ばれる現象で、「き」や「す」のような音が、無声の子音に挟まれると、声帯が震えなくなるために起こります。聞き取りが苦手な学習者は、文字どおりの母音を探してしまうばかりに、かえって混乱しがちです。この仕組みを知っておくだけで、シャドーイングの精度は目に見えて上がります。
cards.en: Have you ever noticed that the vowels of Japanese desu and masu are in fact barely audible? This is a phenomenon called vowel devoicing: when sounds like ki or su are sandwiched between voiceless consonants, the vocal cords stop vibrating. Learners who find listening hard tend to get more confused precisely because they search for the vowel as written. Simply knowing this mechanism noticeably raises the accuracy of your shadowing.

っておくだけで、シャドーイングの

words.defJa: 時代や社会の大きな流れ

cards.ja: 話の説得力は、個々の出来事より、その背後にある潮流を示せるかどうかで決まる。たとえば十九世紀の欧州を語るとき、民族主義の高まりという大きな流れを一本の線として置けば、統一運動も独立運動も同じ文脈で整理できる。聞き手は、事実の量ではなく、筋道の見通しに納得するのだ。講演に先立って、まず大きな流れを一文で示しておくことをお勧めする。そうすれば、細部の話がどこへ向かうのか、聞き手は迷わずについてこられる。
cards.en: A talk's persuasiveness is decided less by individual events than by whether you can show the currents behind them. When discussing nineteenth-century Europe, for instance, if you set the rise of ethnic nationalism down as a single line, unification movements and independence movements can both be organized in the same context. Listeners are convinced not by the volume of facts but by a clear view of the thread. Before a lecture, I recommend first stating the large flow in a single sentence. Then listeners can follow without getting lost about where the details are heading.

ruby: わずについてこられる。
cards.tipJa: 「時代の潮流」。海の流れから、社会の大きな方向へ広がった語。
cards.enTarget: A talk's persuasiveness is decided less by individual events than by whether you can show the currents behind them.

words.defJa: 対立や競争が激しさを増すこと

cards.ja: 半導体の先端製造をめぐる米国と中国の対立が、このところ一段と激化している。輸出規制の強化に対し、中国は重要鉱物の輸出管理で応じており、双方の措置が連鎖して歯止めがかからない構図が続く。一方、各国の企業は調達先の分散を急ぎ、供給網の再編を余儀なくされている。熾烈な技術競争は短期では収まらないとの見方が専門家の間で強い。最先端の製造装置を持つ国々が、今後の交渉の鍵を握ることになりそうだ。
cards.en: The confrontation between the United States and China over advanced semiconductor manufacturing has been intensifying further of late. In response to tighter export controls, China has answered with export management of key minerals, and a pattern of measures chaining one after another with no brake continues. Meanwhile, companies in each country are hurrying to diversify their sourcing and are being forced to reorganize their supply chains. Experts widely hold that the fierce technological competition will not subside in the short term. The countries that hold the most advanced manufacturing equipment look set to hold the key to future negotiations.

cards.tipJa: 「対立が激化する」。戦争・競争・議論が激しさを増す。
cards.enTarget: The confrontation between the United States and China over advanced semiconductor manufacturing has been intensifying further of late.

words.defJa: 時間をかけて深く考えること

cards.ja: 熟考とは、時間をかけて深く考えることである。だが、考える時間が長いほど結論が良くなるとは限らない。人は迷うほどに、自分の選ばなかった選択肢の魅力を過大に見積もり、選んだものへの満足を下げてしまうからだ。ゆえに、深く考えることの本当の価値は、結論を完璧にすることではなく、判断の根拠を自分の言葉で説明できる状態をつくることにあるのではないか。根拠を言葉にしておけば、のちに結果が裏目に出ても、自分を責める代わりに、次の決断力の足場にできる。
cards.en: Deliberation means thinking deeply and taking time. But a longer time spent thinking does not necessarily mean a better conclusion. The more people waver, the more they overestimate the appeal of the options they did not choose and lower their satisfaction with the one they chose. Hence the true value of thinking deeply lies not in making the conclusion perfect but in creating a state in which you can explain the grounds of your judgment in your own words. If you put the grounds into words, then even if the result backfires later, instead of blaming yourself you can make it a foothold for your next decisiveness.

をつくることにあるのではないか。
cards.tipJa: 「熟考を重ねる」。「熟慮」とほぼ同義だが、やや硬い。
cards.enTarget: Deliberation means thinking deeply and taking time.

words.defJa: 文章をじっくり読み込むこと

cards.ja: 国語の力を伸ばしたいなら、まず一冊を熟読するに限ります。速く読む技術は便利ですが、速読は情報を拾うのに向いていて、文章の組み立てや言葉の選び方を味わうのには向きません。じっくり読むときは、気になった一文に線を引き、なぜそう書かれたのかを自分に問います。それを数ページ続けるだけで、文章の骨格が見えるようになり、書く力にもつながります。ときには注釈を読み比べたり、音読で響きを確かめたりするのも効果的です。
cards.en: If you want to build your Japanese language ability, nothing beats first reading a single book carefully. Speed-reading skills are handy, but speed reading suits picking up information and not savoring how a text is built or how words are chosen. When you read slowly, underline a sentence that caught your attention and ask yourself why it was written that way. Just continuing that for a few pages lets you see the skeleton of the writing and also links to the ability to write. It is also effective at times to compare annotations or to confirm the sound by reading aloud.

words.defJa: 昔の中国語の文章を日本語風に読むもの

cards.ja: 高校の授業で漢文が出てきたとき、返り点ってなんだこれ、って思ったよね。中国語の語順を日本語の読み順に並べ替えるための印なんだけど、慣れるまではまるでパズルを解くかのようだった。でも今思うと、あれは外国語を翻訳せずに「読み下す」という、ものすごく独特な技術だったんだよね。現代語訳に頼らずに白文を読めた人は、それだけで一目置かれたと思う。今でもあの響きを聞くと、少し背筋が伸びる。
cards.en: When kanbun came up in high school class, I remember thinking, what on earth are these return marks? They are marks for rearranging Chinese word order into Japanese reading order, but until I got used to them it was as if I were solving a puzzle. Looking back now, though, it was an extraordinarily unique technique of reading a foreign language off without translating it. Someone who could read unpunctuated text without relying on a modern-language translation earned respect for that alone, I think. Even now, when I hear that sound, my back straightens a little.

words.defJa: 一つの漢字を書く画の数

cards.ja: 漢字の画数は、学習者の負担を考えるうえで、一つの手がかりになる。「一」はわずか一画、「鬱」は二十九画で、その差は書く手間にそのまま表れる。しかし、画が多いことが、そのまま難しさを意味するとは限らない。構成要素のまとまりを捉えられれば、多画の字も、少画の字の組み合わせとして記憶できるからである。覚える側の工夫次第で、漢字仮名交じり文を読む負担も、数字の重さほどには変わらない。
cards.en: A kanji's stroke count is one clue in thinking about the burden on learners. The character for one has just one stroke and the character for depression has twenty-nine, and that difference shows directly in the effort of writing. However, having many strokes does not necessarily mean being difficult. If you can grasp the clusters of components, even many-stroke characters can be memorized as combinations of few-stroke characters. Depending on the learner's ingenuity, the burden of reading mixed kanji-kana writing does not change as much as the weight of the numbers suggests.

cards.tipJa: 画数は辞書で漢字を引く手がかりにもなる。
cards.enTarget: A kanji's stroke count is one clue in thinking about the burden on learners.

words.defJa: 植民地支配から独立を目指す運動

cards.ja: 歴史の発表で独立運動を扱うときは、年表を並べる前に、誰が何に抗議したのかを一言で言えるようにしておくといい。たとえばインドなら、塩の行進のように、象徴的な行動が運動の性格を一目で伝える。聞き手は細かい年号より、場面の絵を覚えている。だから、話の最初と最後に同じ場面を置くと、構成にまとまりが出る。民族主義の高まりを背景にした運動なら、その熱を伝える場面を選ぶとよい。
cards.en: When covering an independence movement in a history presentation, it helps to be able to say in one phrase who protested what before lining up a chronology. For India, for example, a symbolic action like the Salt March conveys the character of the movement at a glance. Listeners remember the picture of a scene rather than detailed dates. So placing the same scene at the beginning and end of the talk gives the structure coherence. For a movement against a backdrop of rising ethnic nationalism, choose a scene that conveys that heat.

cards.enTarget: When covering an independence movement in a history presentation, it helps to be able to say in one phrase who protested what before lining up a chronology.

words.reading: かんじかなまじりぶん
words.defJa: 漢字とひらがなを混ぜて書く日本語の書き方

cards.ja: 日本語の文章は、漢字と仮名を組み合わせた漢字仮名交じり文で書かれる。世界の文字体系のなかでも珍しいこの方式は、漢字が意味の核を、仮名が文法の骨組みを担うという分業によって成り立っている。そのおかげで、読み手は文を一字ずつ追わなくても、漢字を拾うだけで大意をつかむことができる。もっとも、その便利さは、膨大な漢字の習得という代償と引き換えである。画数の多い字を前に、学習者が立ちすくむのも無理はない。
cards.en: Japanese texts are written in mixed kanji-kana writing, which combines kanji and kana. This system, unusual even among the world's writing systems, rests on a division of labor in which kanji carry the core of meaning and kana the framework of grammar. Thanks to that, readers can grasp the gist just by picking out the kanji, without following the sentence one character at a time. However, that convenience comes at the price of mastering a huge number of kanji. It is no wonder learners freeze before characters with many strokes.

cards.enTarget: Japanese texts are written in mixed kanji-kana writing, which combines kanji and kana.

words.defJa: 自分では意識されない心の働き

cards.ja: 寝る前に考えてた悩みが、朝起きたら急に解決してること、ない？それって潜在意識が働いてるって言われるよね。でも正直、その言葉ってちょっと便利すぎて、うさんくさく感じるときもあるんだ。心理学的には、自分では気づかないまま処理されてる情報がある、くらいの意味にとどめたほうが安全だと思う。熟睡できた翌朝ほど、あの現象は起きやすい気がするから、まずは睡眠を削らないのが先だよね。
cards.en: Haven't you had the experience of a worry you were thinking about before bed suddenly resolving when you wake up in the morning? People say the subconscious is at work in that. But honestly, the word is a bit too convenient, and sometimes it feels a little shady to me. I think it is safer to keep its meaning to something like psychology's idea that some information gets processed without our noticing. Since that phenomenon seems likelier the morning after a sound sleep, the first thing is not to cut into your sleep.

ruby: してること、ない？それって
cards.tipJa: 「無意識」と近いが、通俗的な語。学術では慎重に使う。
cards.enTarget: People say the subconscious is at work in that.

words.defJa: 古文や漢文を現代の言葉に訳したもの

cards.ja: 古典を読むとき、いきなり原文に挑む必要はありません。まず現代語訳で全体の筋をつかみ、そのあとで原文に戻ると、語の響きや言い回しの面白さがぐっと見えてきます。ただし、訳文は訳者の解釈を通した一つの読みにすぎないことを、頭の片隅に置いておきましょう。同じ一節でも、訳者が違えば、印象がまったく変わる場合があります。二つ以上を読み比べ、注釈も併せて見ると、原文のふくらみがわかります。
cards.en: When reading the classics, you do not need to tackle the original text right away. First grasp the overall plot through a modern-language translation, then return to the original, and the sound of the words and the charm of the phrasing come into view all the more. Keep in mind, though, that a translated text is merely one reading filtered through the translator's interpretation. Even for the same passage, the impression can change completely if the translator differs. Comparing two or more and looking at the annotations together shows the fullness of the original.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: のふくらみがわかります。
cards.tipJa: 古典の原文に対する訳文。「注釈」とセットで使う。
cards.enTarget: First grasp the overall plot through a modern-language translation, then return to the original, and the sound of the words and the charm of the phrasing come into view all the more.

words.reading: げんじょういじばいあす
words.defJa: 今の状態を変えたくない心理的な偏り

cards.ja: 人は、いまの状態を変えることのリスクを、実際より大きく見積もる傾向があります。これを現状維持バイアスといい、転職や引っ越しを迷い続ける人ほど、無意識のうちにこの影響を受けています。ある企業では、制度を「自動加入」にして、辞退したい人だけが手続きをする形にしたところ、加入率が大きく上がりました。選択肢の初期設定を変えるだけで、人の行動は変わります。これは環境設計の発想そのものです。
cards.en: People tend to estimate the risk of changing their present state as greater than it really is. This is called status quo bias, and people who keep wavering over changing jobs or moving are unconsciously under its influence. At one company, when the scheme was changed to automatic enrollment, with only those who wished to opt out going through a procedure, the enrollment rate rose sharply. Just by changing the default of the options, people's behavior changes. This is the very idea of environment design.

cards.tipJa: 「現状維持の偏り」。初期設定を変えると人の選択が動く。
cards.enTarget: This is called status quo bias, and people who keep wavering over changing jobs or moving are unconsciously under its influence.

words.defJa: 災害や戦争が後に残した傷あと

cards.ja: ベルリンの街を歩くと、第二次世界大戦の爪痕が、いまも壁の弾痕や、崩れたまま残された教会の塔に刻まれていることがわかります。ただ、傷は物の形だけにとどまらず、人々の記憶や、世代を越えて伝わる沈黙にも残ります。街が東西に分けられた時代の経験も、そこに重なります。だからこそドイツでは、過去を隠すのではなく、あえて目に見える形で保存する道が選ばれてきました。その痕跡をどう次の世代へ手渡すかが、いまも大きな課題です。
cards.en: Walking through Berlin, you can see that the scars of the Second World War are still carved into the bullet holes in walls and the church tower left standing in ruins. But the wounds do not stop at physical form; they also remain in people's memories and in a silence handed across generations. The experience of the era when the city was divided into east and west overlaps there. That is exactly why Germany has chosen the path of preserving the past in a visible form instead of hiding it. How to hand those traces on to the next generation is still a major challenge.

ruby: まれていることがわかります。ただ、
なります。だからこそドイツでは、
cards.tipJa: 「戦争の爪痕」。災害や戦争が残した、目に見える傷あと。
cards.enTarget: Walking through Berlin, you can see that the scars of the Second World War are still carved into the bullet holes in walls and the church tower left standing in ruins.

words.defJa: 唐の都の発音に基づく漢字の音読み

cards.ja: 漢字の音読みには、伝わった時代の違う層がある。奈良時代から平安時代にかけて、唐の都・長安の発音をもとに伝えられた漢音は、比較的新しい層とされる。「行」をコウと読む行進がその例で、ギョウと読む行事は、それ以前に入った呉音に当たる。同じ字でも熟語によって読みが分かれるのは、こうした伝来の層が今も残っているためだ。熟字訓のように音とは無関係な読みと並べると、日本語の読みの多層ぶりがいっそうはっきりする。
cards.en: Kanji's on readings have layers that arrived in different eras. Kan-on, brought over between the Nara and Heian periods based on the pronunciation of Chang'an, the Tang capital, is regarded as a relatively new layer. The word for marching, with the character for go read ko, is an example, whereas the word for an event, read gyo, corresponds to go-on, which came in earlier. That the same character is read differently depending on the compound is because these layers of transmission remain today. Setting them beside readings unrelated to sound, like whole-word kun readings, makes the layered nature of Japanese readings all the clearer.

words.defJa: 心を乱し、苦しみを生む欲や怒りなど

cards.ja: 除夜の鐘は、人間が持つ百八の煩悩を払うために撞かれると言われる。百八という数の由来には諸説あり、六つの感覚器官に、好・悪・平の区別、浄と染、過去・現在・未来を掛け合わせる説などが知られている。仏教では、心を乱し苦しみを生む働きを総称してこう呼び、欲望だけでなく怒りや無知も含む。年齢を問わず、年越しには鐘の音に耳を澄まし、無心に一年を振り返る参拝者の列が、各地の寺で見られる。
cards.en: The bells of New Year's Eve are said to be struck to dispel the one hundred eight worldly passions that humans have. There are various theories about the origin of the number 108, and one known theory multiplies the six sense organs by the distinctions of liking, disliking and neutrality, purity and defilement, and past, present and future. In Buddhism, the workings that disturb the mind and produce suffering are collectively called this, and it includes not only desire but also anger and ignorance. Regardless of age, lines of worshippers who listen to the sound of the bells and look back over the year with an empty mind can be seen at temples around the country.

words.defJa: 廃された王政がもう一度復活すること

cards.ja: 世界史の論述で王政復古を扱うときは、清教徒革命からの流れを、一続きの物語として書くことが肝心です。クロムウェルの死に伴って政治が不安定になり、一六六〇年にチャールズ二世が帰国して王位に就きました。ただし、議会の力は強まったままで、課税や軍隊をめぐる王の権限には制限がかかります。つまり、王政は戻っても、元の絶対王政に戻ったわけではないのです。この区別が答案の質を分けます。
cards.en: When you deal with the Restoration in a world-history essay, it is essential to write the flow from the Puritan Revolution as one continuous line. With Cromwell's death, politics became unstable, and in 1660 Charles II returned and took the throne. However, Parliament's power remained strong, and limits were placed on the king's authority over taxation and the army. In other words, even though the monarchy returned, it did not return to the former absolute monarchy. This distinction separates the quality of answers.

words.defJa: きわめて激しいさま

cards.ja: 人工知能向けの半導体をめぐり、熾烈な開発競争が続いている。各社は、演算性能だけでなく、消費電力あたりの性能でも優位を築こうと、巨額の投資を重ねている。勝者の座は固定されておらず、昨日の先頭が、今日の追う側に回る例も珍しくない。競争は設計だけでなく、製造や素材、人材の確保にまで及び、国家間の対立を激化させる要因にもなっている。最後に勝ち残るのは、最も速い会社より、変化に最も早く適応した会社だろう。
cards.en: A fierce development race continues over semiconductors for artificial intelligence. Companies are piling on huge investments in order to build an advantage not only in computing performance but also in performance per unit of power consumption. The winner's seat is not fixed, and it is not rare for yesterday's front-runner to become today's chaser. The competition extends beyond design to manufacturing, materials, and securing talent, and it is also a factor intensifying conflict between nations. The one that survives in the end will probably be the company that adapted fastest to change rather than the fastest company.

words.reading: しょうがいがくしゅう
words.defJa: 一生を通じて学び続けること

cards.ja: うちの母、六十五歳で定年を迎えたあと、近所の大学の公開講座に通い始めてさ。生涯学習って言うと立派に聞こえるものの、本人は「家にいるより面白いから」って言うだけなんだよね。でも、むしろそれがいいんだと私は思う。何かを学ぶ理由を、役に立つかどうかだけで測っていると、いつか続かなくなる。好奇心の延長で動いているほうが、結局は長く、深く続くし、本人いわく毎日が気づきの連続で、ちっとも飽きないらしい。
cards.en: After retiring at sixty-five, my mother started attending a nearby university's open lectures. Lifelong learning sounds impressive, but all she says is that it's more fun than staying home. But I think that's exactly what's good about it. If you measure your reason for learning by whether it's useful or not, it stops lasting. Moving along as an extension of curiosity ends up lasting longer and deeper, and by her own account every day is a string of realizations, and she never gets bored.

words.defJa: 現代の発音に近づけた仮名の使い方

cards.ja: 現代仮名遣いは、戦後の一九四六年に定められた表記の約束を引き継ぎ、発音に近づけた表記のきまりです。たとえば「てふてふ」は「ちょうちょう」に、「思ふ」は「思う」になりました。ただ、助詞の「は」「へ」「を」だけは、発音と表記がずれたまま残っています。これは、文の構造を目で見て素早く判断できるという利点を優先した結果と考えられます。歴史的仮名遣いを知ると、そのずれの理由が見えてきます。
cards.en: Modern kana orthography inherits the conventions of writing set down in 1946 after the war and is a set of rules that brings spelling closer to pronunciation. For example, tefutefu became chouchou, and omofu became omou. Only the particles ha, he, and wo, however, remain with a gap between pronunciation and spelling. This is thought to be the result of prioritizing the advantage of being able to judge sentence structure quickly by eye. Once you know historical kana orthography, the reason for that gap comes into view.

words.reading: せいぞんしゃばいあす
words.defJa: 生き残った例だけを見て判断を誤ること

cards.ja: 成功者の共通点を調べたからといって、同じようにうまくいくとは限りません。その原因の一つが、生存者バイアスです。成功した人の話だけが目に入り、同じことをして失敗した大勢の人は見えなくなるため、成功の要因を実際より単純に考えてしまうのです。第二次世界大戦中、帰還した爆撃機の弾痕を調べた統計学者が、弾痕のない部分こそ補強すべきだと見抜いた話は、洞察力の例として有名です。
cards.en: Just because you have studied what successful people have in common does not mean you will succeed the same way. One cause of this is survivorship bias. Only the stories of those who succeeded catch your eye, and the many who did the same thing and failed become invisible, so you end up thinking of the factors of success as simpler than they really are. The story of the statistician who examined the bullet holes in returning bombers during the Second World War and saw that the parts without holes should be reinforced is famous as an example of insight.

words.defJa: 心身がすり減ってぐったり疲れること

cards.ja: 長期にわたる在宅介護で、心身ともに疲弊してしまう人は少なくありません。体力が削られるだけでなく、自分の時間が失われ、社会との接点が細っていくことが、疲れをいっそう深くします。ここで大切なのは、頑張りで乗り切ろうとせず、早い段階で外部の支援を使うことです。放っておくと、燃え尽き症候群にもなりかねません。介護の経験者ほど、助けを求めることが続けるための技術だと口をそろえます。
cards.en: Over long periods of home nursing care, quite a few people end up exhausted in body and mind. Not only is physical strength worn down, but one's own time is lost and contact with society thins out, which makes the tiredness deeper still. What matters here is not trying to get through on effort but using outside support at an early stage. Left alone, it may even become burnout syndrome. The more experienced the caregiver, the more they say in unison that asking for help is a skill for keeping going.

words.defJa: 自分たちとは別の民族

cards.ja: 古代中国の王朝にとって、北方の遊牧民は、常に安全保障上の課題であった。漢は匈奴との間で戦争と和親を繰り返し、のちの王朝も異民族への備えとして長城を築き、補強した。一方で、彼らは単なる脅威ではなく、朝貢や交易、人材の登用を通じて、中国社会に深く入り込んだ存在でもある。のちに元や清朝を樹立した例は、その関係の複雑さを象徴する。長城は壁であると同時に、交流が生まれる接点でもあったのである。
cards.en: For the dynasties of ancient China, the nomads of the north were always a security problem. The Han repeated war and peace-and-kinship arrangements with the Xiongnu, and later dynasties too built and reinforced the Great Wall as a defense against foreign peoples. At the same time, they were not merely a threat but also became entities deeply embedded in Chinese society through tribute, trade, and the recruitment of talent. The later founding of the Yuan and Qing dynasties symbolizes the complexity of that relationship. The Great Wall was a wall and, at the same time, a point of contact where exchange arose.

cards.en: More and more people open social media, see the successes of their peers, and are seized by a sense of impatience that makes their hands stop. Psychology has repeatedly pointed out that comparison with others lowers self-esteem. The troublesome part is the vicious cycle in which the more anxious you get, the less you can concentrate on the task in front of you and the harder it is to produce results. Left alone, it can lead to a loss of energy and exhaustion of body and mind. What works here is the habit of writing down three things you accomplished today at the end of the day.

words.defJa: 古いことを学び、新しい知恵を得ること

cards.ja: 『論語』にある「故きを温ねて新しきを知る」は、四字熟語で温故知新と呼ばれる。古いものをただ懐かしむのではなく、そこから現在に通じる知恵を引き出せ、という教えである。歴史を学ぶ意味もここにあるが、過去をそのまま当てはめれば、状況の違いを見落としかねない。大切なのは、昔の出来事を、いまの課題を映す鏡として読み直す態度であろう。そう読むとき、歴史は繰り返すという言葉も、単なる諦めではなく、一つの警告になる。
cards.en: The phrase from the Analects, 'warm up the old and know the new,' is called onko chishin as a four-character idiom. It teaches that one should not merely feel nostalgia for the old but draw out of it wisdom that speaks to the present. This is also the point of studying history, but applying the past as it is risks overlooking differences in circumstances. What matters is the attitude of rereading past events as a mirror that reflects today's problems. Read that way, the saying that history repeats itself becomes not mere resignation but a warning.

cards.en: The American Declaration of Independence is dated July 4, 1776, so that day becomes Independence Day every year, right? But actually, the resolution of independence itself was adopted on July 2, and what was approved on the 4th was the text of the declaration. The central drafter was Jefferson, and he is said to have written the famous passage that all men are created equal. Yet, contrary to that ideal, slavery continued at the time, and this document would also be cited again and again in later calls for national self-determination.

words.defJa: 異端を取り調べ、罰した教会や国家の裁判

cards.en: From the medieval to the early modern period, the Inquisition, in which the Catholic Church investigated deviations in faith, was carried out in various parts of Europe. Notably, the inquiry established in the latter half of the fifteenth century in Spain under the initiative of the crown is known for having severely pursued converts from Judaism and Islam. Investigations accompanied by torture spread fear through society, encouraged silence, and left deep scars. Modern historical research, while continuing to debate the scale of the victims, is trying to clarify the reality of the system from the historical sources.

For example, with that famous photo of the blue and gold dress, how colors looked split depending on how people imagined the surrounding light. Which means the world we see may be half an inference made by the brain. When you think about it, treating your own eyes as absolute is a bit dangerous, isn't it?

words.defJa: 石油の供給や価格の急変による経済の混乱

cards.ja: 一九七三年の第四次中東戦争をきっかけに、アラブの産油国が石油の輸出を制限し、一部の国には禁輸を宣言して、価格を大幅に引き上げました。これが第一次石油危機です。石油の大半を輸入に頼っていた日本は、物価の急上昇に見舞われ、トイレットペーパーの買いだめ騒ぎまで起きました。しかし、この経験が、省エネルギー技術の開発を促し、日本の産業構造を変える転機にもなります。危機が、のちの強さの出発点になったという見方もあります。
cards.en: Triggered by the Fourth Middle East War in 1973, the Arab oil-producing countries restricted oil exports, declared an embargo against some countries, and raised prices sharply. This was the first oil crisis. Japan, which relied on imports for most of its oil, was hit by soaring prices, and even a rush to hoard toilet paper occurred. Yet this experience also spurred the development of energy-saving technology and became a turning point that changed Japan's industrial structure. Some also see the crisis as the starting point of later strength.

For instance, even if you line up technical terms for someone hearing them for the first time, they cannot organize the content, and in the end nothing remains. So before you speak, draw a line in your head between what the listener knows and does not know. That decides eighty percent of an explanation's quality.

words.defJa: 迷いから覚めて真実に気づくこと

cards.en: What is called awakening in Indian thought is not waking in the morning but noticing that you had been inside a dreamlike assumption. The word Buddha itself means the awakened one. In the Vedanta tradition too, it is taught that the true self has been there unchanged from the start and becomes visible when the veil of ignorance is removed. In other words, it is not gaining something new but nothing other than the falling away of superfluous things called worldly passions. This view quietly changes the meaning of the discipline of seeking truth.

cards.enTarget: What is called awakening in Indian thought is not waking in the morning but noticing that you had been inside a dreamlike assumption.

words.defJa: いつでも変わらない正しい道理

cards.ja: ウパニシャッドには、「真理のみが勝つ」という言葉があり、現代インドの国章にも刻まれています。ここで言われているのは、日常の事実の正しさに限らず、変わらない根源的なあり方です。ヴェーダーンタは、その根源がブラフマンと呼ばれ、私たち一人ひとりの内なる自己アートマンと、実は同じものだと説きます。この見方に立てば、それは外で探すものではなく、気づくものになります。目覚めの体験が語られるとき、この発想が静かに貫いています。
cards.en: The Upanishads have the phrase 'truth alone triumphs,' which is also engraved on India's national emblem today. What is meant here is not limited to the correctness of everyday facts but the unchanging, fundamental mode of being. Vedanta teaches that this root is called Brahman and is in fact the same as each of our inner selves, the Atman. From this view, it is not something to seek outside but something to notice. This idea runs quietly through whenever the experience of awakening is spoken of.

words.defJa: 物事が始まるきっかけ

cards.ja: 世界史の因果関係を問う問題では、発端と引き金を区別して書くと、答案が引き締まります。たとえば第一次世界大戦の場合、一九一四年のサライェヴォ事件は直接の引き金にすぎず、背景には列強の同盟関係や、民族主義の高まりがありました。原因をどこまでさかのぼるかで、歴史の見え方は大きく変わります。だから答案では、短期の原因と長期の原因を、時間の幅を分けて整理しましょう。大きな潮流と一つの事件を、きちんと切り分けることが肝心です。
cards.en: In questions that ask about causal relationships in world history, distinguishing between the inception and the trigger makes your answer tighter. In the case of the First World War, for example, the 1914 Sarajevo incident was merely the direct trigger, and in the background were the alliances among the great powers and the rise of ethnic nationalism. How far back you trace the causes changes how history looks. So in your answer, sort short-term causes and long-term causes by separating the time spans. It is essential to cleanly separate the large current from the single incident.

words.defJa: 知的能力を平均百の数値で表したもの

cards.ja: 知能指数は、平均を百とし、集団内での位置を示すように設計された数値である。この数値が、学校の成績や職業上の成功と、ある程度の相関関係を持つことは、多くの研究が示している。しかし、それは人間の価値を測る物差しではなく、特定の課題における得点の指標にすぎない。そのうえ、数値は時代とともに平均が上がり、基準を作り直さなければならなかったという事実も、この指標の相対性を物語る。
cards.en: The IQ is a figure designed with a mean of one hundred to indicate a person's position within a group. Many studies show that this figure has a certain degree of correlation with school grades and occupational success. But it is not a yardstick for measuring a person's worth; it is merely an index of scores on particular tasks. Moreover, the fact that averages rose over the decades and norms had to be rebuilt also speaks to the relativity of this index.

words.defJa: 新しい考えを思いつく力

cards.ja: 企業の間で、社員の発想力を高める研修が広がっている。異なる部署の人を集め、互いの仕事を体験させる時間を設ける例が目立つ。専門が違えば、同じ問題でも見え方が大きく異なるため、思いがけない組み合わせが生まれやすいという。ただ、年齢や職種を問わず参加できる場を作るだけでは足りず、失敗を許す空気がなければ、提案は出てこない。独創性を評価する仕組みを整えることが欠かせないと、専門家は指摘する。
cards.en: Training programs to boost employees' creative ideation are spreading among companies. Examples stand out in which people from different departments are gathered and given time to experience each other's work. When specialties differ, the same problem looks very different, so unexpected combinations are said to arise easily. However, it is not enough merely to create a place anyone can join regardless of age or job type; without an atmosphere that tolerates failure, proposals will not come out. Experts point out that it is indispensable to set up a system that evaluates originality.

words.defJa: 石などに刻まれた文章

cards.ja: 歴史の資料のなかでも、碑文は、後世の編集を受けていない一次史料として、特に重んじられます。たとえば、古代エジプトのロゼッタ・ストーンには、同じ内容が三つの文字で刻まれており、これが象形文字の解読の鍵になりました。シャンポリオンは、一八二二年に、この石を手がかりに解読に成功します。ただし、刻まれた文章は、権力者が残したい物語に偏りがちなので、誰が何のために刻んだのかを考え、他の資料と突き合わせる必要があります。
cards.en: Among historical sources, inscriptions are especially valued as primary sources that have not undergone later editing. For example, the Rosetta Stone of ancient Egypt has the same content carved in three scripts, and this became the key to deciphering hieroglyphs. Champollion succeeded in the decipherment in 1822 using this stone as a clue. However, since carved texts tend to be biased toward stories the powerful wanted to leave, you must consider who carved it and for what purpose and cross-check against other sources.

words.reading: はってんとじょうこく
words.defJa: 経済や産業がまだ発展途中にある国

cards.ja: 発展途上国という呼び方は、豊かな国が先頭にいて、残りがその後を追うという一本の階段を前提にしている。しかし、この前提そのものが、植民地支配の爪痕を見えにくくしてきたという批判がある。資源を安く輸出させられ、産業の芽を育てる余地を奪われた地域にとって、遅れとは能力の問題ではなく、構造の帰結にほかならない。近年は、「グローバル・サウス」という語が、この単線的な図式への反発として使われることが多い。一つの言葉の選択が、世界の見方を静かに決めている。
cards.en: The label developing country presupposes a single staircase on which rich countries are in the lead and the rest follow behind. But there is criticism that this premise itself has made the scars of colonial rule harder to see. For regions made to export resources cheaply and deprived of room to nurture the seeds of industry, being behind is nothing other than the consequence of structure, not a problem of ability. In recent years, the term Global South is often used as a reaction against this single-track scheme. A single choice of words quietly decides how we see the world.

words.reading: しゃかいけいやくせつ
words.defJa: 国家の正当性を人々の合意に求める考え

cards.ja: 社会契約説は、国家の正当性を、人々の合意に求める考え方である。ホッブズは、自然状態を「万人の万人に対する闘争」と見て、秩序のために強い主権者への服従を説いた。これに対しロックは、人々が政府に権力を預けたのだから、政府が約束を破れば抵抗してよいと論じる。やがてこの発想は、アメリカの独立宣言やフランスの人権宣言へと流れ込み、近代の民主化の土台となった。契約という比喩は、権力は天から与えられるものではないという宣言でもあった。
cards.en: Social contract theory is the idea of seeking the legitimacy of the state in people's agreement. Hobbes saw the state of nature as a war of all against all and preached obedience to a strong sovereign for the sake of order. In contrast, Locke argued that since people entrusted power to government, they may resist if the government breaks its promise. In time this idea flowed into the American Declaration of Independence and the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and became the foundation of modern democratization. The metaphor of a contract was also a declaration that power is not something granted from heaven.

words.defJa: 物事を白か黒かの二つだけで考える癖

cards.ja: 白黒思考とは、物事を善か悪か、成功か失敗かの二つに分けて考える癖である。この癖が強いと、一度の失敗を「自分は全部だめだ」という全否定に結びつけてしまいやすい。実際には、世界は灰色の濃淡に満ちており、成功と失敗のあいだに無数の段階がある。にもかかわらず、人が単純な区分を好むのは、複雑さに耐える負担を、無意識に減らそうとするからではないか。その負担を少し引き受けてみることが、柔軟な考え方を育てる最初の一歩になる。
cards.en: Black-and-white thinking is the habit of dividing things into two, good or bad, success or failure. When this habit is strong, one tends to link a single failure to total self-negation, as in I am completely useless. In reality, the world is full of shades of gray, and there are countless stages between success and failure. Even so, is the reason people prefer simple divisions that they are trying, unconsciously, to reduce the burden of enduring complexity? Taking on a little of that burden is the first step in nurturing flexible thinking.

words.defJa: 経験によって脳の仕組みが変わる性質

cards.ja: 脳は大人になってからも、経験に応じて、神経回路のつながり方を作り替えることができます。この性質を神経可塑性と呼びます。たとえばピアノなどの楽器の練習を数年続けると、指の動きを制御する領域が変化することが、研究で示されています。ただし、変化には、反復と十分な睡眠が欠かせず、短期間の詰め込みでは定着しにくいのです。だから、勉強は一晩の詰め込みではなく、毎日少しずつ、積み重ねるに限ります。
cards.en: Even in adulthood, the brain can remake how its neural circuits connect in response to experience. This property is called neuroplasticity. Research has shown, for example, that if you keep practicing an instrument such as the piano for several years, the region controlling finger movements changes. However, repetition and sufficient sleep are indispensable for change, and cramming in a short period hardly takes hold. So when it comes to study, nothing beats piling it up little by little every day rather than cramming in one night.

words.defJa: 中国で官僚を選ぶために行われた試験

cards.ja: 中国の科挙ってさ、役人になるための試験なんだけど、とにかく倍率が桁違いだったんだよね。隋の時代に始まって、清の末期の一九〇五年まで、千三百年ほど続いたらしい。身分を問わず挑戦できる建前だったから、才能のある人が出世できる仕組みとして評価されることも多い。でも、実際には、受験の準備に何年も費やせる余裕のある家の人が、圧倒的に有利だった。仕組みの美しさと現実の格差を、一緒に見ておくのが大事だよね。
cards.en: The Chinese keju is an exam for becoming an official, and the competition rate was just off the charts. Apparently it began in the Sui era and lasted about thirteen hundred years, until 1905 at the end of the Qing. Because the public line was that anyone could take it regardless of status, it's often praised as a system through which talented people could rise. But in reality, people from families who could afford years of exam preparation had an overwhelming advantage. It's important to look at the beauty of the system and the actual inequality together.

words.defJa: 短い時間だけ情報を保っておく記憶

cards.ja: 短期記憶は、電話番号を一度聞いて、ダイヤルするまで覚えておくような、短時間の保持に使われる記憶です。容量は限られており、昔の研究では七つ前後、のちの研究では四つ前後だとされています。ここで役立つのが、情報を「まとまり」にして数を減らす工夫です。たとえば、〇九〇一二三四五六七八なら、三桁、四桁、四桁の三つに分けるだけで、覚えやすさは大きく変わります。電話番号に限らず、近年の知見を使えば、暗記全般の効率も上がります。
cards.en: Short-term memory is the memory used for brief retention, such as hearing a phone number once and keeping it in mind until you dial. Its capacity is limited, said to be around seven items in older research and around four in later research. What helps here is the device of reducing the count by turning information into chunks. For example, 09012345678 changes greatly in how easy it is to remember simply by splitting it into three chunks of three, four, and four digits. Not only phone numbers: if you use recent findings, the efficiency of memorization in general also improves.

words.reading: いしのうえにもさんねん
words.defJa: 辛抱すればいつか報われる

cards.ja: 「石の上にも三年」は、冷たい石でも三年座り続ければ温まる、という意味から、辛抱すれば必ず報われることをたとえる。しかし、現代の働き方では、何でも我慢せよという教えとして使うことは危うい。続ける価値のある場所を見極める眼があって初めて、この言葉は力を持つからである。続けることと、しがみつくことは違う。続けた末に得た熟達が、自分の意志で選んだ道の上にあるかどうかを、時折問い直したい。
cards.en: 'Even a stone becomes warm after three years' compares to the idea that if you endure, you will surely be rewarded, from the notion that even a cold stone warms if you sit on it for three years. In today's ways of working, however, it is risky to use it as a teaching that you must put up with anything. This is because the saying gains force only when you have the eye to judge which place is worth staying in. Continuing and clinging are different. I want to ask myself from time to time whether the mastery gained after continuing lies on a path I chose by my own will.

words.defJa: 生まれつきの脳の特性による発達の偏り

cards.ja: 発達障害のある人と話すとき、相手の特性に合わせた伝え方を意識すると、会話がぐっと楽になる。たとえば、曖昧な指示を避け、「いつまでに、何を、どの程度」を具体的に言葉にする。口頭だけでなく、メモや図を併用して、記憶の負担を減らすことも有効だ。的確な指示は、注意散漫になりやすい人にとって、安心して動ける足場になる。こうした工夫は、特定の人に限らず、聞き手全員にわかりやすい話し方の基本にもなる。
cards.en: When speaking with a person who has a developmental disorder, being conscious of a way of communicating suited to the other's traits makes conversation much easier. For example, avoid vague instructions and put into words concretely by when, what, and to what extent. It is also effective to use notes and diagrams in addition to speech to reduce the load on memory. Precise instructions become a foothold on which people prone to distraction can move with peace of mind. These adjustments, not limited to particular people, also become the basics of a way of speaking that is clear to all listeners.

words.defJa: 「ように」などで直接たとえる表現

cards.ja: 文章指導の場では、「雪のように白い肌」のような直喩は、読み手に一瞬で絵を思い浮かべさせると説明される。「ように」「ごとし」を使って、二つのものを直接比べる表現で、比喩の一種である。一方で、使い古された言い回しは、決まり文句と同じで、かえって印象を弱めてしまう。自分だけの発見を一つの比較に込められるかどうかが、上達の分かれ目だとされる。観察が先にあって、言葉があとから追いかけるのが理想だ。
cards.en: In writing instruction, a simile like 'skin white as snow' is explained as letting the reader picture an image in an instant. It is an expression that directly compares two things using words like 'as' or 'like,' a kind of metaphor. On the other hand, a worn-out phrase is the same as a stock phrase and rather weakens the impression. Whether you can pack your own discovery into one comparison is said to be the dividing line of improvement. The ideal is for observation to come first and words to chase after it.

words.reading: ひゃくぶんはいっけんにしかず
words.defJa: 何度も聞くより一度見るほうが確かだ

cards.ja: 「百聞は一見にしかず」は、人から百回聞くより、自分の目で一度見るほうが確かだ、という意味のことわざです。出典は『漢書』で、前漢の将軍・趙充国の言葉として伝わっています。とはいえ現代では、見たものだけを信じると、かえって見かけにだまされる場面もあります。そこで大切になるのが、見たあとに、その背景を確かめ直す知的好奇心です。ことわざは、疑う習慣とセットで読むと、いっそう深みが出ます。
cards.en: The proverb 'seeing once beats hearing a hundred times' means that seeing something once with your own eyes is more reliable than hearing about it a hundred times from others. Its source is the Book of Han, and it is handed down as the words of the Former Han general Zhao Chongguo. Even so, in the modern age there are occasions when believing only what you see leaves you fooled by appearances. What matters then is the intellectual curiosity to check the background again after seeing. A proverb gains even more depth when read together with the habit of doubting.

words.defJa: 睡眠不足が少しずつ積み重なること

cards.ja: 毎日少しずつ睡眠が足りない状態が続くと、睡眠負債が積み上がります。これは、借金のように、返さなければ集中力や判断力が確実に落ちていく状態です。厄介なのは、本人が慣れてしまい、自分の能力の低下に気づきにくいことです。眠っている間に記憶を整理する海馬の働きも、不足のしわ寄せを受けかねません。週末の寝だめで一部は取り戻せても、完全には返済できないと考えられています。
cards.en: If a state of getting a little too little sleep every day continues, sleep debt piles up. Like a loan, if you do not repay it, concentration and judgment steadily decline. The troublesome part is that the person gets used to it and finds it hard to notice a decline in their own ability. The work of the hippocampus, which organizes memories while we sleep, could also bear the strain of the shortfall. It is thought that even if you recover part of it by sleeping in on weekends, you cannot repay it completely.

words.defJa: 声を出すこと。声の出し方

cards.ja: 声が通らないと悩む人は、声を出す前に、まず呼吸を見直すとよいでしょう。発声の基本は、喉ではなくお腹で息を支え、一定の量を安定して吐き出すことです。試しに、ろうそくの火を揺らさない程度の強さで、「あー」と十秒間伸ばしてみてください。そのとき肩に力が入っていないか、顎が上がっていないかも、あわせて確かめます。この練習を毎日の積み重ねとして続ければ、場の広さに応じて音量を調整できるようになります。
cards.en: If you worry that your voice does not carry, it is a good idea to review your breathing before you produce any sound. The basis of vocalization is to support the breath with your belly, not your throat, and to let out a constant amount steadily. As a trial, stretch out an ah for ten seconds with just enough force not to make a candle flame waver. At that time, also check whether your shoulders are tense and whether your chin is lifted. If you keep up this practice as a daily accumulation, you will be able to adjust your volume according to the size of the room.

cards.en: The longer people stay active in the professional world, the less they neglect their studies. Many skilled craftspeople are said to practice the basic movements again every morning, no matter how high their reputation becomes. This is not only to maintain technique but because each time you repeat the basics, new realizations arise. It may not be about adding special things but about deepening the ordinary. People who do not doubt small accumulations end up going far.

cards.ja: 外交の場では、合意の中身を明言せず、含みを持たせる言い方が頻繁に用いられる。首脳会談のあとで「協力の拡大を示唆した」と報じられるとき、それは確定ではなく、方向性だけを伝えている。読む側は、ほのめかしと断定の違いを見分けて、記事の温度を測る必要がある。語尾の一つひとつに、書き手の確信の度合いが現れる。弱い表現を、強い意味に読み替えてしまうことが、誤解の入口である。
cards.en: In diplomatic settings, ways of speaking that leave the content of an agreement unstated and carry overtones are used frequently. When a report after a summit says it suggested an expansion of cooperation, that is not a confirmed fact and conveys only a direction. Readers need to distinguish a hint from an assertion and gauge the temperature of the article. The degree of the writer's confidence shows in each sentence ending. Reading a weak expression as a strong meaning is the entrance to misunderstanding.

cards.en: The tendency to gather only information that supports your own ideas and to take contrary information lightly is called confirmation bias. When search results and posts on the internet are rearranged to suit the user's tastes, this tendency may well strengthen. Researchers point out that the habit of deliberately reading opinions from the opposite position and looking for holes in your own reasoning raises the quality of judgment. However, since people unconsciously avoid that work, it is desirable to build it in as a mechanism.

cards.ja: 日本語の文では、目的語は多くの場合「を」で示され、動詞の直前に置かれます。ところが英語では、動詞のあとにそれを置くのが基本の並びです。基本の並びは単純なものの、母語の癖が出やすく、語順の混乱は日本人学習者の作文によく現れます。たとえば「私はリンゴを食べる」を、頭の中で一語ずつ置き換えると、逆の順序になってしまいます。直訳に頼らず、語順そのものを一つの型として覚えるのが近道です。
cards.en: In Japanese sentences, the object is in most cases marked by wo and placed right before the verb. In English, however, the basic order puts the object after the verb. Though the basic order is simple, habits of the mother tongue easily show through, and confusion of word order often appears in Japanese learners' compositions. For example, if you replace 'I eat an apple' one word at a time in your head, you end up with the reverse order. The shortcut is to memorize word order itself as a single pattern without relying on literal translation.

You tend to think you'll sleep soundly if you lie down, but that's not so much the case.

cards.en: Postwar Britain, under the slogan 'from the cradle to the grave,' pushed ahead with building a welfare state, including the creation of the National Health Service. The vision of social security presented in the Beveridge Report became its foundation. But the economic stagnation of the 1970s highlighted the weight of the fiscal burden, and politicians who argued for scaling back welfare appeared. How far to support that system is a debate that continues even now over the burden of taxation and the level of benefits.

For example, the English Parliament opened a path to restraining power by preventing the king from taxing at will. The slogan 'no taxation without representation' later became the banner of the American independence movement. Who decides taxes and how is a question at the heart of democratization.

Experts see the ability to look again at the process of learning, not just to memorize knowledge, as the foundation of later lifelong learning.

cards.en: Research findings keep appearing in behavioral economics that an accumulation of small actions produces large differences in the long run. For example, people who set up an automatic daily deposit of a small amount of savings are said to see assets grow more easily without being swayed by mood. It takes time for results to appear, and many people run out of energy partway. For that reason, experts recommend methods that support continuation through environment design, such as recording progress to make it visible.

words.defJa: 栄えることと衰えること

cards.ja: 歴史を読んでいて面白いのは、国や家の盛衰が、意外と同じ筋書きをたどることなんだよね。強い時期は、外から見ても内から見ても勢いがあって、批判する人すら少ない。ところが、その自信が過信に変わったとたん、小さな綻びを誰も直さなくなる。興亡って、結局は、自分たちを見る目が曇るかどうかの話なんだと思う。だからこそ、勝っているときこそ、疑う人から得られる知見を大事にしたい。
cards.en: What is interesting in reading history is that the rise and fall of nations and houses follows a surprisingly similar plot. In a strong period, there is momentum seen from outside and inside, and even people who criticize are few. But the moment that confidence turns into overconfidence, no one fixes small flaws anymore. Ultimately, I think the story of ascent and ruin is about whether the eye that sees ourselves clouds over. That is exactly why, when we are winning, we want to value the insights that come from those who doubt.

America stopped exporting oil to Japan, and Japan was cornered into having to do something before its stockpile ran out. But looking a bit more calmly, diplomatic options had already narrowed before that, and there were problems in the military's judgment too. Even if that was the decisive blow, I think we get the causes of history wrong unless we look at the accumulation leading up to it. Placed beside the story of the oil crisis, the fearfulness of resources is easy to see.

Still, there is no need to make this a source of guilt. Rather, some see having unknown books close at hand as functioning as a storehouse of intellectual curiosity. When the time to read comes, one of them will suddenly start to shine before your eyes.

words.defJa: 生産手段を共有し、平等を目指す思想

cards.ja: 社会主義は、産業革命がもたらした貧富の格差への応答として、十九世紀のヨーロッパに広がった。工場主が生産手段を握り、労働者がわずかな賃金で働く構造を、人々は不正義と受け取ったのである。ただ、同じ名で呼ばれる思想の幅は広く、国家による管理を重んじる潮流もあれば、協同組合による自治を重んじる潮流もあった。この多様さを見落とすと、のちに現れた体制の失敗が、思想全体の失敗として語られかねない。
cards.en: Socialism spread through nineteenth-century Europe as a response to the gap between rich and poor brought by the Industrial Revolution. People took the structure in which factory owners held the means of production and workers labored for meager wages to be unjust. However, the range of thought called by the same name is wide, and there were currents that valued state management as well as currents that valued self-government by cooperatives. If this diversity is overlooked, the failure of regimes that appeared later could be told as the failure of the whole idea.

words.defJa: 機械や工場が実際に動いていること

cards.ja: 半導体工場の稼働率は、景気の先行きを占う指標として、投資家に注目されている。最先端の工場では、一度止めると再開に多くの時間と費用がかかるため、需要が落ちても生産を続けることが多い。一方、需要が急に増えたときには、設備の増強が間に合わず、供給の不足が長引く。こうした硬直性が、汎用品の市場も含めて、半導体市場に周期的な好不況の波を生む。工場の動きは、世界経済の体温を映す鏡でもある。
cards.en: The operating rate of semiconductor factories draws investors' attention as an indicator for foretelling the economy's prospects. At cutting-edge factories, because restarting once stopped takes much time and expense, production often continues even when demand falls. On the other hand, when demand suddenly rises, equipment expansion cannot keep up, and supply shortages drag on. This rigidity produces cyclical waves of boom and bust in the semiconductor market, general-purpose goods included. The movements of factories are also a mirror reflecting the body temperature of the world economy.

words.defJa: 知りたい、わかりたいという知的な好奇心

cards.ja: 知的好奇心は、教えられなくても、人が自然に持っている力です。けれども、点数や評価ばかりを重んじる環境では、この力はしだいにしぼんでいきます。逆に、「なぜだろう」という問いを歓迎される場にいると、学ぶこと自体が楽しみになります。大人になってからも、気になったことを一つ深掘りして調べる習慣は、生涯にわたって学び続ける入り口になります。まずは、今日見かけた小さな不思議を、一つだけ調べてみましょう。
cards.en: Intellectual curiosity is a power people naturally have even without being taught. However, in an environment that values only scores and evaluations, this power gradually withers. Conversely, when you are in a place where the question 'why is that?' is welcomed, learning itself becomes a pleasure. Even as an adult, the habit of digging deeper into one thing that caught your interest is the entrance to learning throughout life. First, try looking into just one small mystery you came across today.

cards.en: Neurons in the brain are not directly connected to each other but pass on information by handing over neurotransmitters across gaps called synapses. Dopamine and serotonin are well known and are said to be involved in regulating motivation and mood. They are sometimes simply called happiness hormones, but their actual effects differ depending on the receiving cell and the neural circuit. For that reason, researchers are cautious about explaining emotions by a particular substance alone.

words.defJa: 芸事や武道を繰り返し学ぶこと

cards.ja: 能や歌舞伎に限らず、日本の伝統芸能では、稽古という言葉が、単なる練習以上の意味を持つ。古い型を繰り返し身体に入れ、師の動きを自分の動きに移し替えていく過程である。それを重ねるうちに、型は意識せずとも出てくるようになり、そのとき初めて自由が生まれると、多くの芸の世界で語られる。「守破離」という考え方も、この段階を表している。基本を徹底して身につけた熟達者だけが、型を超えられるのである。
cards.en: Not only in Noh and Kabuki, in Japan's traditional performing arts the word keiko carries more than the meaning of mere practice. It is the process of taking old forms into the body through repetition and transferring the master's movements into your own. It is said in many artistic worlds that as you accumulate this, the forms come out without conscious thought, and only then does freedom arise. The idea of shu-ha-ri also expresses these stages. Only an expert who has thoroughly mastered the basics can go beyond the forms.

words.defJa: 何のためにやるのかという自覚

cards.ja: 話し方を磨きたい人に、まず問いたいのは、その話に目的意識があるかどうかだ。説得したいのか、共感してほしいのか、それとも情報を淡々と渡したいのか。目的に応じて、選ぶ言葉も、話す順序も、声の調子も変わる。目的を曖昧にしたまま話し始めると、どれほど流暢でも、聞き手には何も残らない。話す前に、一文で「この話の目的は〜だ」と言えるようにしておくだけで、発声の練習以上の効果が出る。
cards.en: What I first want to ask people who want to polish their speaking is whether their talk has a sense of purpose. Do you want to persuade, win sympathy, or simply hand over information plainly? Depending on the purpose, the words you choose, the order you speak in, and the tone of your voice all change. If you start talking with the purpose vague, however fluent you are, nothing remains for the listener. Just making yourself able to say in one sentence before speaking, 'the purpose of this talk is to...', has an effect beyond vocal practice.

words.defJa: 信号を受けて伝える脳や神経の細胞

cards.ja: 神経細胞は、入力を受け取る樹状突起と、出力を送る軸索を持つ、細長い形の細胞です。ほかの細胞から信号を受け取り、刺激の強さに応じて、一定の強さを超えると電気の信号を発して次へ伝えます。この単純な仕組みが、八百億を超える数で結びつくことで、思考や記憶が生まれます。一つひとつは単純でも、つながり方に意味が宿る、という点では、言葉の成り立ちにも似ています。だからこそ、脳は、部分の足し算では説明できないのです。
cards.en: A nerve cell is an elongated cell with dendrites that receive input and an axon that sends output. It receives signals from other cells and, depending on the strength of stimulation, once a certain threshold is exceeded, fires an electrical signal and passes it on. When this simple mechanism is linked in numbers exceeding eighty billion, thought and memory arise. In that meaning resides in how things are connected even though each is simple, it resembles how language is formed. That is exactly why the brain cannot be explained by adding up parts.

words.reading: しんせいろーまていこく
words.defJa: 中世から近世にかけて続いたドイツ中心の帝国

cards.ja: 神聖ローマ帝国は、「神聖でも、ローマでも、帝国でもない」と皮肉られた国です。九六二年、オットー一世が教皇から皇帝の冠を受けたことを起点とし、ドイツを中心に、多数の領邦が緩やかにまとまる国でした。王位継承も世襲ではなく、有力諸侯による選挙で決まったため、皇帝の権力は強まりにくかったのです。この分権的な性格が、のちのドイツの統一が遅れた背景として、試験でもよく問われます。
cards.en: The Holy Roman Empire was a state mocked as neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire. Starting from Otto I receiving the imperial crown from the pope in 962, it was a state in which numerous territories centered on Germany were loosely joined. Because succession to the throne was decided not by heredity but by election among powerful princes, the emperor's power was hard to strengthen. This decentralized character is often asked on exams as a background to the later delay of German unification.

words.defJa: 原文の語を一つずつそのまま訳すこと

cards.ja: 英語の勉強では、直訳に頼りすぎると、不自然な文ができあがります。たとえば「お疲れさま」を「あなたは疲れている」と英語にしても、相手をねぎらう意味は伝わりません。ここで必要なのは、日本語の意味を捉えたうえで、英語の発想に組み替える作業です。そのためには、母語話者がよく使う型を、決まり文句として丸ごと覚えるのが近道です。訳すのではなく、場面と結びつけて持ち帰るのがコツです。
cards.en: In studying English, relying too much on literal translation produces unnatural sentences. For example, even if you render 'otsukaresama' into English as 'you are tired,' the meaning of acknowledging the other person's effort does not come across. What is needed here is the work of grasping the meaning in Japanese and then recasting it in English thinking. To that end, the shortcut is to memorize, as stock phrases, the patterns native speakers often use as whole units. The trick is not to translate but to take them home tied to their situations.

words.defJa: 言語と社会の関係を調べる学問

cards.ja: 社会言語学って、ことばを人間関係とか立場から見る学問なんだけど、日常に使える発見が多くて好きなんだよね。たとえば、同じ人でも、友達と話すときと、上司と話すときでは、語尾も話すスピードも違う。あれって無意識に相手に応じて切り替えてるんだって。方言を隠したくなる気持ちも、実は社会の評価と結びついてる。ことばの違いは、ただの癖じゃなくて、人間関係の地図みたいなものなんだと思う。
cards.en: Sociolinguistics is a field that looks at language through human relationships and social position, and I like it because it has lots of discoveries you can use in daily life. For example, even the same person differs in sentence endings and speaking speed when talking with friends and when talking with a boss. Apparently we unconsciously switch depending on the other person. The urge to hide a dialect is also tied to social evaluation. I think differences in speech aren't just quirks but something like a map of human relationships.

words.defJa: 神経細胞がつながって作る情報処理の道筋

cards.ja: 人間の脳には、八百億を超える神経細胞があり、それらが複雑な神経回路を作って情報を処理している。近年は、この回路の配線図を、顕微鏡画像から再構成する研究が進んでいる。たとえば、小さな昆虫の脳の全体像が描かれ、行動との対応が調べられるようになった。配線図が得られたとしても、それだけで心の働きがわかるわけではないが、研究者は、地図ができたこと自体が大きな前進だとみている。
cards.en: The human brain has over eighty billion neurons, and they form complex neural circuits to process information. In recent years, research reconstructing the wiring diagram of these circuits from microscope images has advanced. For example, the whole picture of a small insect's brain has been drawn, and its correspondence with behavior can be examined. Even if a wiring diagram is obtained, it does not by itself tell us how the mind works, but researchers regard the very existence of a map as a major step forward.

words.reading: りっけんくんしゅせい
words.defJa: 憲法によって君主の権限が制限される政治制度

cards.ja: 王がいる国だからといって、王が望むままに税を課し、法律を決められるとは限らない。立憲君主制では、君主の権限は憲法によって制限され、議会や政府との関係の中に位置づけられる。ただし、君主にどこまで実際の政治権力を認めるかは、国や時代によって異なる。王朝の系譜をたどるだけでは見えてこないのは、権限をめぐる交渉と、長い時間をかけた制度の変化である。政治体制の名前を覚えるにとどまらず、誰が決定し、誰がそれを止められるのかを問うことが、歴史を読む上で欠かせない。
cards.en: Just because a country has a king does not mean that he can levy taxes and make laws as he pleases. Under a constitutional monarchy, the monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and situated in a relationship with parliament and government. However, the extent of the monarch's actual political power differs by country and period. Tracing royal dynasties alone does not reveal negotiations over powers or institutional changes that unfold over long periods. When reading history, it is essential to go beyond memorizing the names of political systems and ask who makes decisions and who can stop them.

words.defJa: 経済上の制限で相手国に圧力をかけること

cards.ja: 経済制裁は、武力を使わずに相手国に圧力をかける手段として、二十世紀に広く使われるようになりました。たとえば一九三五年、イタリアがエチオピアに侵攻したとき、国際連盟は、イタリアへの制裁を決めました。しかし、石油が対象外だったため、効果は限定的で、侵攻を止めることはできませんでした。この失敗は、制裁の実効性が、対象となる品目や参加国の足並みに大きく左右されるという教訓を残しました。そして、制裁が戦争の発端になった例もあります。
cards.en: Economic sanctions came to be widely used in the twentieth century as a means of pressuring another country without force. In 1935, for example, when Italy invaded Ethiopia, the League of Nations decided on sanctions against Italy. However, because oil was excluded, the effect was limited and the invasion could not be stopped. This failure left the lesson that the effectiveness of sanctions depends greatly on the items targeted and the unity of the participating countries. And there are also cases where sanctions became the origin of a war.

words.defJa: 要するに言えば

cards.ja: 小論文では、結論を急ぐばかりに根拠が薄くなる失敗が目立ちます。この問題を端的に言えば、読み手の疑問に先回りして答えていないということです。たとえば「A社が成功した」と書くだけでは、「なぜ」という疑問が残ります。そこで、一文のあとに「その理由は〜」と理由を足すだけで、説得力は大きく上がります。こうした型を身につけると、試験本番でも、的確に論点を押さえられます。
cards.en: In short essays, the failure of hurrying to a conclusion so that the grounds grow thin stands out. Putting this problem simply, you are not answering the reader's questions ahead of time. For example, just writing that company A succeeded leaves the question of why. So just adding a reason after a sentence, saying the reason is, greatly raises persuasiveness. Once you master such a pattern, you can pin down the points precisely even on exam day.

words.defJa: あきらめずに粘り続ける性質

cards.ja: 長期的な成功を予測する性格特性として、才能よりも、粘り強さが注目されている。心理学者のアンジェラ・ダックワースは、困難があっても目標に向かって努力を続ける力を「グリット」と呼び、研究と著書で広めた。ただし、この概念をめぐっては、他の性格特性との区別が曖昧だという批判もある。また、努力を続ける価値のある目標かどうかを見極める力は、目標設定そのものの質に関わるという指摘もある。
cards.en: Tenacity, more than talent, is drawing attention as a personality trait that predicts long-term success. The psychologist Angela Duckworth called the power to keep making effort toward a goal even in the face of difficulty 'grit' and popularized it through research and a book. However, there is criticism that the concept is vague in its distinction from other personality traits. There is also a view that the ability to judge whether a goal is worth continuing for relates to the quality of goal setting itself.

words.defJa: 精神面での粘り強さや耐える力

cards.ja: スポーツの世界では、精神力という言葉が、勝敗を分ける要素としてよく語られる。しかし、競技者を対象にした研究では、成功する選手ほど、気合に頼るのではなく、緊張を前提にした手順を持つ傾向が示された。たとえば、試合前の呼吸法や、失敗した直後に切り替える短い合図などである。つまり、それは生まれつきの強さというより、練習で身につけた習慣の総和だと考えられる。目標設定の精密さも、その一部をなす。
cards.en: In the world of sports, the word mental strength is often discussed as a factor that decides victory or defeat. But in research on athletes, a tendency was shown that the more successful the player, the less they rely on sheer spirit and the more they have procedures that presuppose nervousness. Examples are breathing methods before a match and short cues for switching right after a mistake. In other words, it is thought to be less innate strength than the sum of habits acquired through practice. The precision of goal setting also forms a part of it.

words.defJa: 対立する者を組織から排除すること

cards.ja: 一九三〇年代のソ連では、スターリンによる大規模な粛清が行われ、党幹部や軍の将校、一般市民に至るまで、多くの人々が逮捕され、処刑された。「大テロル」と呼ばれるこの時期の犠牲者の数は、史料の公開が進んだ現在も、研究者の間で議論が続く。それは、恐怖によって社会の服従を引き出す手段として使われ、人々の間に深い不信を残した。のちに、この時代の記録を掘り起こして新しい知見を加える作業が、歴史家だけでなく、遺族たちによっても続けられてきた。
cards.en: In the Soviet Union of the 1930s, a large-scale purge by Stalin was carried out, and many people, from party officials and military officers to ordinary citizens, were arrested and executed. The number of victims of this period, called the Great Terror, is still debated among researchers even now that the release of sources has advanced. It was used as a means of drawing obedience from society through fear and left deep distrust among people. Later, the work of digging up records of this era and adding new findings has been carried on not only by historians but also by bereaved families.

words.defJa: 場の雰囲気や相手の気持ちを察する

cards.ja: 日本語の会話では、空気を読むことが、言葉の意味そのものより重んじられる場面があります。たとえば「ちょっと難しいですね」は、字面では程度を述べているだけですが、実際には断りの合図として働くことが多いのです。だから、日本語を学ぶ人にとっては、相槌のタイミングや沈黙の長さも、大事な情報になります。もっとも、察しすぎて本音を言えなくなると、今度は会議が前に進みません。結局、察する力と、はっきり言う勇気は、両方そろって初めて意味を持つのです。
cards.en: In Japanese conversation, there are occasions when reading the room is valued more than the meaning of the words themselves. For example, 'it's a little difficult' merely states a degree on its face but in practice often works as a signal of refusal. So for people learning Japanese, the timing of back-channel responses and the length of silences also become important information. That said, if you read the signals too much and can no longer say what you really think, the meeting will in turn go nowhere. In the end, the ability to read between the lines and the courage to speak plainly gain meaning only when both are present.

words.defJa: 物事が始まる最初の手がかり

cards.ja: 戦争の端緒を探すとき、歴史家は、最初の発砲という目に見える出来事だけでなく、その前に積み重なった緊張にも目を向ける。第一次世界大戦の始まりを一九一四年のサライェヴォ事件に置く見方は、わかりやすいが、同盟関係や軍備競争を軽く扱う恐れがある。起点とは、因果の鎖のどの輪をそう呼ぶかという、解釈の問題でもある。しかも、事件と結果のあいだの相関関係が、そのまま原因を意味するわけではない。したがって、起点の選び方に、その歴史家の問いが映る。
cards.en: When searching for the origin of a war, historians look not only at the visible event of the first shot but also at the tensions that built up before it. The view that places the start of the First World War at the 1914 Sarajevo incident is easy to understand but risks treating alliances and the arms race lightly. A starting point is also a matter of interpretation: which link of the chain of causation you choose to call it. Moreover, a correlation between an incident and an outcome does not mean as it stands that it is the cause. Therefore the way a historian chooses the starting point reflects that historian's question.

words.defJa: まず結論を述べる言い方

cards.ja: 結論から言うと、人の話が長く感じられる最大の原因は、情報の量ではなく、順序にあります。最初に結論を示すと、聞き手は、あとに続く説明を、その結論の理由として整理しながら聞けるからです。逆に、経過から話し始めると、聞き手は、どこへ向かうのかわからないまま、記憶に負担をかけ続けます。この型は、メールや会議に限らず、日常の雑談にも使えます。端的に言えば、順序を変えるだけで、話は驚くほど軽くなるのです。
cards.en: To start with the conclusion, the biggest reason a person's talk feels long lies not in the amount of information but in the order. If you present the conclusion first, listeners can organize the explanation that follows as reasons for that conclusion while listening. Conversely, if you begin with the course of events, listeners keep burdening their memory without knowing where it is heading. This pattern can be used not only in emails and meetings but also in everyday chat. Put simply, just changing the order makes a talk surprisingly light.

words.defJa: 情報を記憶できる形に変えること

cards.ja: 記憶の第一段階は、符号化と呼ばれます。これは、目や耳から入った情報を、脳が扱える形に変換する過程です。深く考えながら処理した情報ほど、のちに思い出しやすいことが、多くの実験で示されています。たとえば単語を覚えるときに、文字の形を眺めるより、その意味を自分の生活と結びつけるほうが、長く残ります。意味づけをせずに流すと、短期記憶から消えかねないので、知見に基づいて、情報を一度ことばにして海馬へ渡すのが、勉強の要です。
cards.en: The first stage of memory is called encoding. It is the process of converting information that enters through the eyes and ears into a form the brain can handle. Many experiments have shown that information processed while thinking deeply is easier to recall later. For example, when memorizing a word, linking its meaning to your own life lasts longer than gazing at the shape of the letters. If you let it flow past without giving it meaning, it may vanish from short-term memory, so the key to studying, based on research findings, is to put information into words once and pass it on to the hippocampus.

words.defJa: 漢字を書くときの画の順序

cards.ja: 文部省が一九五八年にまとめた「筆順指導の手びき」は、学校で漢字を教える際の目安とされてきたが、唯一の正解を定めたものではない。手びき自体が、示した順序以外を誤りとするものではないという趣旨を述べている。それでも、試験や書道の場では、書き順が評価の対象になる場合がある。画数の多い字ほど、無理なく書ける順序を体で覚える意味は大きい。正しさより、再現できる流れを身につけることが先だ。
cards.en: The 'Handbook for Stroke Order Instruction,' compiled by the Ministry of Education in 1958, has served as a guideline when teaching kanji in schools but does not fix a single correct answer. The handbook itself states the intent that orders other than those it shows are not to be treated as mistakes. Even so, in exams and calligraphy, the order of strokes can become an object of evaluation. The more strokes a character has, the greater the meaning of learning with the body an order you can write without strain. Acquiring a flow you can reproduce comes before correctness.

words.defJa: 落ち込んだ状態から元に戻る

cards.ja: 失敗したあと、すぐに立ち直る人といつまでも引きずる人の差は、才能より、失敗の語り方にあると私は考えている。「自分はだめだ」という白黒思考の代わりに、「この方法は合わなかった」と、主語を行動に移してみる。それだけで、人格への全否定が、改善できる課題へと姿を変える。話し方の稽古でも、緊張で言葉に詰まった自分を責めず、次の一回のために、気づきを一つだけ持ち帰るようにしたい。
cards.en: I believe that the difference between people who recover quickly after failure and those who keep dragging it along lies in how they talk about the failure, more than in talent. Instead of black-and-white thinking like I am hopeless, try shifting the subject to the action: this method did not suit me. That alone turns a total denial of one's character into a problem that can be improved. Even in speaking practice, I want to avoid blaming myself for freezing from nerves and take home just one realization for the next attempt.

words.defJa: 型にはまっていて新味のない

cards.ja: 紋切り型の表現は、書き手を安心させるが、読み手を眠らせる。「心に残る一日だった」「大きな影響を受けた」といった言い回しは、誰が書いても通用するため、誰にも届かない。その代わりに、場面の具体的な細部、たとえば雨の匂いや、相手の指先の動きを一つだけ書いてみる。すると、同じ内容でも、不思議と書き手の目の存在が立ち上がる。省察の深い文章は、必ず具体的な細部に支えられている。
cards.en: Formulaic expressions reassure the writer but put the reader to sleep. Phrases like 'it was a memorable day' and 'I was greatly influenced' work no matter who writes them, and so reach no one. Instead, try writing just one concrete detail of the scene, such as the smell of rain or a movement of the other person's fingertips. Then, even with the same content, the presence of the writer's eye strangely rises into view. Writing with deep reflection is always supported by concrete details.

words.defJa: 西暦より前の時代

cards.ja: 紀元前という数え方は、ふつうの年表とは逆向きに進みます。たとえば前三三一年は、前三二〇年より古く、数字が大きいほど過去にさかのぼります。ここで注意したいのは、西暦一年の前が前一年であり、ゼロ年が存在しないことです。暦が作られた時代の欧州に、ゼロの概念がまだ定着していなかったためだとされ、歴史学の知見でもそう説明されます。だから、前三世紀は、前三〇〇年から前二〇一年を指します。
cards.en: The BC way of counting runs in the opposite direction from an ordinary chronology. For example, 331 BC is earlier than 320 BC, and the larger the number, the further back in the past. What to note here is that the year before AD 1 is 1 BC and that there is no year zero. This is said to be because the concept of zero had not yet taken hold in Europe when the calendar was made, and historical findings explain it that way too. So the third century BC refers to 300 through 201 BC.

words.defJa: つながりのある思想や血筋の流れ

cards.ja: インド哲学の系譜をたどると、ヴェーダの時代から、ウパニシャッド、そして六つの正統派哲学へと、思想が少しずつ深まっていくのが見えてきます。仏教やジャイナ教は、そこから離れた別の流れとして、同じ時代に生まれました。大切なのは、これらが互いに影響を与え合い、対話しながら発展した点です。たとえば真理とは何か、自己とは何かという問いは、立場が違っても共有されていました。系統を一本の線で覚えず、対話の網として見ると、全体がつかみやすくなります。
cards.en: If you trace the lineage of Indian philosophy, you can see thought deepening little by little from the Vedic age to the Upanishads and then the six orthodox schools. Buddhism and Jainism arose in the same period as separate currents departing from it. What matters is that they influenced one another and developed through dialogue. For example, questions such as what truth is and what the self is were shared even across differing positions. If you do not memorize the lineage as one line but see it as a web of dialogue, the whole becomes easier to grasp.

words.reading: ひつぜつにつくしがたい
words.defJa: 言葉ではとても言い表せない

cards.ja: 災害の現場を訪れた記者が、最初に直面するのは、筆舌に尽くしがたい光景をどう言葉にするかという問題である。形容詞を重ねるほど、かえって事実の重みが薄まるため、見えたものを具体的に書く方法が好まれる。たとえば、倒れた本棚と、床に残った子どもの靴という二つの描写だけで、読み手は状況を察する。簡潔明瞭な記述は、感情を押し付けない分、記録としての信頼性を保つ。的確な細部の選び方が、報道文の腕の見せどころだ。
cards.en: What a reporter visiting a disaster site faces first is the problem of how to put into words a sight beyond description. The more adjectives you pile up, the more the weight of the facts thins, so a method of writing concretely what was seen is preferred. For example, with only two depictions, a fallen bookcase and a child's shoe left on the floor, the reader grasps the situation. Clear and concise description, to the extent it does not push feelings, preserves reliability as a record. The choice of precise details is where news writing shows its skill.

words.defJa: 簡単で、はっきりわかりやすいさま

cards.ja: ビジネス文書で求められるのは、簡潔明瞭であることです。一通のメールに依頼を三つ入れると、読み手はどれから手をつけるか迷い、結局どれも後回しにしてしまいます。だから、一通に依頼は一つに限り、件名にも本文の冒頭にもそれを書くのが基本です。そのうえで、期限と、判断に必要な情報だけを添えます。こうして削った文面は、冷たいのではなく、相手の時間への敬意の表れであり、的確な件名がその第一歩になります。
cards.en: What is demanded of business documents is to be clear and concise. If you put three requests in a single email, the reader is unsure where to start and ends up putting all of them off. So the basic rule is to limit each email to one request and to write it in both the subject line and the opening of the body. On top of that, attach only the deadline and the information needed for a decision. A text trimmed this way is not cold but an expression of respect for the other person's time, and a precise subject line is the first step.

words.defJa: 文章を細部まで丁寧に読むこと

cards.ja: 小説を読むのって、速さよりも、一文一文をちゃんと味わう精読のほうが、自分には合ってるんだよね。一ページを三十分かけて読むと、作者がなんでこの言葉を選んだのか、って考える余裕が出てくる。そうすると、直喩とか、ちょっとした言い換えの意図が、急に見えてくるんだ。小説に限らず、論文でも同じで、全部の本をそうは読めないけど、年に数冊だけ、じっくり付き合う本があるといいと思う。
cards.en: When it comes to reading novels, close reading, savoring each sentence properly, suits me better than speed. If you spend thirty minutes on a page, you get room to think about why the author chose this word. Then the intent behind similes and little rephrasings suddenly comes into view. It's the same not only with novels but with papers too; I can't read every book that way, but I think it's good to have a few books a year to spend time with.

words.defJa: 冷戦期の、どちらの陣営にも属さない国々

cards.en: The Cold War term 'Third World' referred to countries that belonged to neither the American camp nor the Soviet camp. When you talk about it, it is good to establish first that the word was originally a term for a political stance rather than one denoting economic poverty. The 1955 Bandung Conference was a symbolic occasion on which Asian and African countries showed solidarity outside the East-West confrontation. If you can explain the difference from the present-day label developing country, the listener's understanding deepens a step.

words.defJa: 他と競って勝つ力

cards.ja: 半導体メーカーの競争力は、設計の巧さだけでなく、製造の歩留まりという地味な数字に大きく左右されます。同じ回路を作っても、不良品の割合が低い工場ほど、一枚のウェハーから取れる製品が増えて、原価が下がるからです。そのため、最先端の工程を持つ企業は、稼働率を高く保つために、巨額の投資を続けています。もっとも、投資だけでは優位は維持できず、技術者の確保と、装置メーカーとの連携が欠かせません。精度の追求が、そのまま企業の体力になるのです。
cards.en: A semiconductor maker's competitiveness depends greatly not just on the cleverness of its design but on the humble figure called manufacturing yield. Even when making the same circuit, the lower a factory's defect rate, the more products can be obtained from a single wafer and the lower the cost. For that reason, companies with cutting-edge processes keep investing huge sums to hold their operating rates high. That said, investment alone cannot sustain an advantage; securing engineers and cooperating with equipment makers are indispensable. The pursuit of precision becomes the company's stamina as it is.

cards.en: It is said that a leading authority in a field is not the person with the most papers but the person who changed how that field poses its questions. Still, even an authority's words are not free of error or bias. It is desirable for the press to convey such statements alongside the findings of other experts. An attitude of respect and one of verification can coexist.

words.defJa: 心の働きの不調による病気

It is also known that the risk of onset rises when sleep debt and overwork pile up. Even so, not a few people hesitate to seek treatment for fear of prejudice. What people around them can do is not make a diagnosis but listen to the end and quietly encourage them to get help. Whether workplaces and schools can create an atmosphere that does not blame people for taking time off also affects the speed of recovery.

words.defJa: 測定や判断がどれだけ正確かの度合い

For this reason, verification in the real environment is indispensable before introduction. Experts point out that AI should be positioned not as a substitute for doctors but as a second pair of eyes that reduces oversights. Combining accumulated findings with on-site judgment is the premise.

In actual conversation, showing a natural sense of distance suited to the relationship matters more than conforming perfectly to the rules. An attitude of savoring, one word at a time, a consideration that cannot be translated literally is the shortcut to learning.

words.defJa: 仏教や儒教で重んじられる聖典

cards.ja: 経典という言葉は、仏教では「きょうてん」、儒教の古典では「けいてん」と読み分けられることがあります。釈迦の教えを弟子たちが伝えたとされる仏教の聖典は、サンスクリット語やパーリ語から、漢訳を通じて日本に伝わりました。そのため、日本の仏教者は、原典ではなく漢文の書物を読み込んできました。この違いを知ると、「同じ書物でも、国によって読み方が違う」という言い方に、深い意味が見えてきます。目覚めを説く教えが翻訳によって広がったのは、真理を伝えようとした人々の粘り強さの結果でもあります。

The Buddhist scriptures, said to be the Buddha's teachings handed down by his disciples, reached Japan via Chinese translation from Sanskrit and Pali. For that reason, Japanese Buddhists have studied books in classical Chinese, not the originals. Knowing this difference reveals deep meaning in the phrase “even the same book is read differently depending on the country.” That teachings that preach awakening spread through translation is also the result of the tenacity of people who tried to convey truth.

words.defJa: 経済のしくみや発展の歴史

cards.ja: 経済史の研究では、近年、各国の長期統計を整理し、数百年にわたる所得の推移を比較する試みが進んでいる。産業革命以前の世界では、一人当たりの所得はほとんど伸びなかったことが、複数の推計から示唆されている。産業革命以降の急成長は、人類史の中でも例外的な出来事と位置づけられる。ただ、数字が残る地域は偏っており、発展途上国の長期データは、いまも不足している。そのため、研究者の間では、結論を急がず、推計の誤差を明示する姿勢が重視されている。
cards.en: In economic history research, attempts have recently advanced to organize long-term statistics of various countries and compare income trends over several centuries. Multiple estimates suggest that in the world before the Industrial Revolution, per-capita income hardly grew. The rapid growth since the Industrial Revolution is regarded as an exceptional event even within human history. However, regions where figures survive are skewed, and long-term data for developing countries is still lacking. For that reason, researchers place importance on not rushing to conclusions and on stating the margin of error in estimates.

A friend of mine was told at first that he was tone-deaf, but he kept singing every day and a few years later even formed a band. I think tenacity can be counted as one of the talents, don't you? I think talent is less a finished thing than a name for something in the middle of being nurtured.

cards.tipJa: 「素質がある」。伸びる可能性としての生まれつきの力。
cards.enTarget: When you say talent or aptitude, you tend to think of something you're born with, but I think it's not only that.

words.reading: けっしょうせいちのう
words.defJa: 経験や学習で蓄えた知識や判断力

cards.ja: 知能は、大きく二つに分けて考えられています。新しい問題を素早く解く力は流動性知能と呼ばれ、二十代でピークを迎えて、その後は緩やかに下がります。一方、結晶性知能は、経験や学習で蓄えた知識と判断力で、六十代になっても伸び続けるとされます。つまり、年齢とともに失われるものばかりではなく、深まる力もあるということです。この違いを知っておくと、知的好奇心を持ち続ける意味が、いっそうはっきり見えてきます。
cards.en: Intelligence is considered to divide broadly into two. The power to solve new problems quickly is called fluid intelligence, which peaks in the twenties and declines gradually afterward. Crystallized intelligence, on the other hand, is knowledge and judgment accumulated through experience and learning and is said to keep growing even into one's sixties. In other words, it is not that everything is lost with age; some powers deepen. Knowing this difference makes the meaning of keeping up intellectual curiosity even clearer.

cards.enTarget: Crystallized intelligence, on the other hand, is knowledge and judgment accumulated through experience and learning and is said to keep growing even into one's sixties.

words.defJa: 文章で読み手を動かす力

cards.ja: 筆力とは、文字の勢いではなく、読み手を最後まで連れていく文章の推進力のことだ。そのために必要なのは、難しい語彙より、一文ごとに問いと答えを小さく積み重ねる構成である。たとえば、最初の一文で疑問を投げ、二文目で意外な事実を示すだけで、読み手は先を知りたくなる。簡潔明瞭な文を重ねても、方向が定まっていなければ、力は生まれない。書く前に、「読み終えた人にどうなってほしいか」を一行で決めておき、目的意識を失わないようにしたい。
cards.en: Writing power is not the vigor of the lettering but the driving force of prose that carries the reader to the end. What is needed for that is not difficult vocabulary but a structure that builds small questions and answers sentence by sentence. For example, just throwing out a question in the first sentence and showing a surprising fact in the second makes readers want to know what comes next. Even if you stack clear and concise sentences, no force arises if the direction is not set. Before writing, I want to decide in one line how I want the person who finishes reading to be changed, and not lose my sense of purpose.

cards.enTarget: Writing power is not the vigor of the lettering but the driving force of prose that carries the reader to the end.

words.defJa: 回りくどくなく、要点をそのまま示すさま

cards.ja: 端的な言い方が上手な人は、話が短いのではなく、不要な部分がない人です。たとえば会議で意見を求められたとき、「賛成ですが、予算だけ再検討が必要です」と言い切れば、聞き手は一度で内容をつかめます。逆に、前置きや言い訳から入ると、肝心の結論が最後まで出てきません。短く話すとは、削る勇気そのものだと私は思っています。だから、話す前に、的確な一文に圧縮する練習を、前置きを抜きにしてやってみましょう。
cards.en: People who are good at putting things directly are not people whose talk is short but people with no unnecessary parts. For example, when asked for an opinion in a meeting, if you state flatly, 'I agree, but the budget needs reconsidering,' the listener grasps the content in one go. Conversely, if you start with preambles and excuses, the crucial conclusion does not appear until the very end. Speaking briefly is itself the courage to cut, I think. So before you speak, try compressing it into one precise sentence, doing so without any preamble.

words.defJa: 一つの道にひたすら励むこと

cards.ja: 仏教でいう精進とは、悟りに向かって怠らず努力を続けることで、六波羅蜜の一つに数えられます。ここで大切なのは、苦行のように自分を追い込むのではなく、ほどよい緊張を保ち続けることです。釈迦は、琴の弦を張りすぎても緩めすぎても良い音が出ないと説いたと伝えられます。現代の仕事や勉強にも、この教えは生きており、粘り強さを支えるのは、極端な頑張りではなく、無理のない継続なのです。
cards.en: In Buddhism, shojin means to keep making effort without slacking toward enlightenment and is counted as one of the six perfections. What matters here is not driving yourself as in ascetic practice but keeping a moderate tension. The Buddha is said to have taught that a lute string produces a good sound neither if it is stretched too tight nor if it is too slack. This teaching is alive in modern work and study too: what supports tenacity is not extreme striving but sustainable continuation.
